teile.einleitung: Namaste is a well-known greeting from India and Nepal. You put your palms together and bow your head slightly. The greeting is friendly and shows respect.
wichtigste: Namaste is a greeting in India and Nepal.
You press your palms flat together in front of your chest, with the fingers pointing up.
You bow your head a little as well.
You do not touch the other person.
Namaste is used both to say hello and to say goodbye.
The word comes from Sanskrit and means roughly “I bow to you”.

abschnitte.text: For Namaste you press both **palms** flat together. The hands are held **in front of the chest**, and the fingers point upwards. You also **bow** your head slightly. Often you say the word “Namaste” at the same time. You do **not touch** the other person. You greet only with your own hands.

The word Namaste comes from **Sanskrit**. Sanskrit is a very old language of India. Many holy texts of the Hindus are written in it. “Namas” means roughly a bow, “te” means to you. Together Namaste means about **“I bow to you”**. The word **Namaskar** is used in a similar way.

You can say Namaste as a **greeting** and as a **farewell**. So it works like “Grüezi” and “Adieu” do for us. People greet friends, older people and strangers this way. Especially towards older people the greeting shows **respect**. In temples, people also greet the gods with this hand position.

Through **yoga**, Namaste has become known all over the world. Many yoga classes, in Switzerland too, end with this greeting. Because you do not touch each other, it is very **hygienic**. During the coronavirus pandemic, politicians in other countries therefore sometimes greeted people with Namaste, too.

gewusst: The hand position in Namaste is also called Anjali Mudra.
In Nepal you hear Namaste almost everywhere in daily life, even on the phone.

teile.einleitung: Someone who belongs to no church and no religious community is called unaffiliated. In Switzerland this group has grown strongly in recent decades. People without a religious affiliation are very different: some believe in nothing supernatural, others in God or a higher power.
wichtigste: Unaffiliated means: you belong to no religious community.
Around 1970 only about 1 per cent of people in Switzerland were unaffiliated.
In 2024, according to the Federal Statistical Office, it was about 37 per cent of people aged 15 and over.
In 2022 the unaffiliated were in the majority in Basel-Stadt and Neuchâtel.
The share was smallest in 2022 in Appenzell Innerrhoden.
Many unaffiliated people celebrate Christmas as a family festival.

abschnitte.text: A **denomination** is a branch of faith, such as Roman Catholic or Evangelical Reformed. Someone who is **unaffiliated** belongs to no church and no religious community. This says nothing yet about what a person believes. Some believe in God or in a higher power without being members. Others do not believe in God, and are often called **atheists**.

Around **1970** only about **1 per cent** of people in Switzerland were unaffiliated. Since then their share has risen strongly. According to the **Federal Statistical Office**, about a third were unaffiliated in 2022, and in 2024 about **37 per cent** of people aged 15 and over. That is more than every third person. Many have left the church, others never became members.

There are big differences between the cantons. In 2022, about 56 per cent in **Basel-Stadt** and about 53 per cent in **Neuchâtel** were unaffiliated, that is, the majority. The share was smallest in **Appenzell Innerrhoden**, at about 15 per cent. Age plays a part too: among 25 to 34 year olds about 42 per cent were unaffiliated, among those over 75 only about 16 per cent.

Many festivals have a religious origin. **Christmas**, for example, is a Christian festival. Many people without a religion celebrate it all the same, as a **family festival** with a tree and presents. Many also enjoy Easter or holidays such as Ascension Day as days off. For important events in life there are now also ceremonies without a priest, for example with independent celebrants.

The **Freethinkers’ Association of Switzerland** speaks up for people who live without religion. It wants a clear **separation of state and church**. Other people feel that the churches take on important tasks for society. In Switzerland the cantons decide how the state and the churches work together. **Freedom of religion** protects everyone: you may belong to a religion or to none.

gewusst: Whoever leaves the church no longer has to pay church tax in most cantons.
The Federal Constitution guarantees that nobody may be forced to join a religious community.

teile.einleitung: State Shinto is the name for the form of Shinto that Japan promoted as a state cult from 1868 to 1945. It put the emperor, the tenno, at the centre as a descendant of a goddess. After the Second World War State Shinto was abolished.
wichtigste: State Shinto arose after the Meiji Restoration of 1868.
Shinto and Buddhism were separated from each other in 1868.
The emperor was regarded as a descendant of the sun goddess Amaterasu.
Visits to shrines were regarded as a patriotic duty, not as religion.
The occupation authority abolished State Shinto in December 1945.
In 1946 Emperor Hirohito denied his divinity.

abschnitte.text: In 1868, after a long rule by the shoguns, power in Japan passed back to the **emperor**. This upheaval is called the **Meiji Restoration**. The new government wanted to make Japan modern and strong. In doing so, **Shinto** was to hold the state together. It became the ideological support of the new state.

For centuries Shinto and Buddhism had been closely mixed in Japan. With the order **shinbutsu bunri** of 1868, kami and Buddhas were separated from each other. As a result many Buddhist temples were damaged. The government now promoted mainly the shrines. At the very top stood the **Ise Shrine**, the sanctuary of the sun goddess **Amaterasu**. She was regarded as the ancestress of the imperial house.

The constitution of **1889** actually guaranteed freedom of religion. The government therefore declared shrine Shinto to be a **state cult** and not a religion. In this way visits to shrines could be demanded of everyone as a patriotic duty. The **Imperial Rescript on Education** of 1890 demanded loyalty to the emperor and respect for parents. It was read out solemnly in all schools.

After Japan’s defeat in the Second World War, the country came under Allied occupation. The **occupation authority** under General **MacArthur** issued the **Shinto Directive** on 15 December 1945. It banned state support for Shinto. The shrines became private religious communities. On 1 January 1946, in a New Year statement, Emperor **Hirohito** denied being a living god.

gewusst: Emperor Hirohito’s statement of 1 January 1946 is often called the “declaration of humanity”.
The Japanese constitution of 1947 expressly separates religion and state.

teile.einleitung: The nazar is a blue glass eye that is regarded as a protective amulet. It is especially common in Turkey. Many people believe that it protects against the “evil eye”.
wichtigste: The nazar is an amulet made of blue glass in the shape of an eye.
It is especially common in Turkey, but also in Greece and the Middle East.
The word “nazar” means gaze.
The amulet is meant to protect against the “evil eye”.
People hang it in the house or the car, or wear it as jewellery.

abschnitte.text: The **nazar** looks like an eye. It usually consists of several layers of **glass**: dark blue on the outside, then white, light blue and a black dot in the middle. The word **“nazar”** comes from Arabic and means **gaze**. In Turkey the amulet is also called **nazar boncuğu**, that is, “gaze bead”.

In many cultures there is a belief in the **“evil eye”**. People imagine that an envious look can bring bad luck. The nazar is meant to **ward off** this look. That is why many people hang it in the **house**, in the **car** or on the pram. Some also wear it as a pendant, bracelet or earring.

The nazar is especially common in **Turkey**, but also in **Greece**, in Cyprus and in the **Middle East**. It is a **folk belief** and does not belong to any particular religion. Today the blue eye is also a popular **souvenir**. For some years there has even been an emoji of its own for it.

gewusst: When a nazar breaks, some people believe that it has caught an evil eye.

teile.einleitung: The Shvetambara are one of the two great branches of Jainism, an ancient religion from India. Their name means “white-clad”, because their monks and nuns wear white robes. The other great branch is called Digambara.
wichtigste: Shvetambara means “white-clad”.
Their monks and nuns wear plain white robes.
The monks of the Digambara, by contrast, wear no clothes.
For the Shvetambara, the 19th Tirthankara, Malli, was a woman.
Some groups wear a mouth cloth so as not to harm small living beings.

abschnitte.text: **Jainism** teaches that you should not harm any living being. This non-violence is called **ahimsa**. Over time the Jains split into two branches. The **Shvetambara** wear plain white robes. The monks of the **Digambara**, the “sky-clad”, give up clothes entirely, as a sign of complete possessionlessness.

The Jains revere 24 **Tirthankaras**, great teachers who showed the way to liberation. For the Shvetambara, **Malli**, the 19th Tirthankara, was a woman. The Digambara, by contrast, see Malli as a man. Behind this lies an important point of dispute: the Shvetambara teach that women too can reach liberation. For the Digambara, according to traditional teaching, this is not possible.

Monks of some Shvetambara groups such as the **Sthanakvasi** wear a **mouth cloth**, the muhpatti. It is meant to prevent small living beings from being swallowed or harmed while speaking or breathing. Many monks also carry a soft broom. With it they sweep the ground before they sit down. Both are an expression of ahimsa.

The two branches tell the life of **Mahavira**, the 24th Tirthankara, differently. According to Shvetambara tradition, Mahavira was married to **Yashoda** and had a daughter. The Digambara teach that he never married. The Shvetambara also have holy scriptures of their own, the **Agamas**.

gewusst: Some Jain monks wear a mouth cloth so that they do not accidentally breathe in small insects.

teile.einleitung: The Maya lived in Central America, in the area of present-day Mexico, Guatemala and Belize. Their religion knew many gods, sacred stories and a precise calendar that was closely tied to their faith.
wichtigste: The Maya worshipped many gods of nature.
Chaac was the god of rain.
The Popol Vuh is the sacred book of the K’iche’ Maya.
According to the Popol Vuh, the gods finally shaped humans from maize.
The hero twins are called Hunahpu and Xbalanque.
At the pyramid of Chichén Itzá, a shadow like a snake appears at the equinox.

abschnitte.text: The Maya believed in many gods who ruled over sky, earth and weather. Especially important was **Chaac**, the god of **rain**. He was often shown with an axe with which he struck lightning. He was especially important for farmers, because **maize** needed rain. The rulers were regarded as go-betweens between humans and the gods.

The **Popol Vuh** is the sacred book of the **K’iche’ Maya** in present-day Guatemala. It tells how the gods created the world and humans. First they tried with clay, then with wood, but these humans did not succeed. Finally they shaped humans from **maize**. That is why maize was sacred to the Maya.

In the Popol Vuh there are two heroes: the twins **Hunahpu** and **Xbalanque**. They descend into the underworld **Xibalba**. There they defeat the lords of the underworld by cunning in a **ball game**. Afterwards they rise to the sky as the **sun and moon**. For the Maya the ball game was also an important religious ritual.

The Maya built great **step pyramids** with temples on top. They observed the stars closely and had a very precise **calendar**. At the great pyramid of **Chichén Itzá**, the edge of the staircase casts a jagged shadow in March and September. It looks like a **snake** gliding down the pyramid.

gewusst: One Maya calendar had 260 days and was used for religious festivals and prophecies.
Millions of Maya still live in Mexico and Guatemala today, and many still speak Maya languages.

teile.einleitung: The Black Madonna of Einsiedeln is one of the best-known holy figures in Switzerland. Every year many pilgrims visit the monastery of Einsiedeln in the canton of Schwyz to see her. The figure shows Mary with the infant Jesus.
wichtigste: The **Black Madonna** stands in the **Chapel of Grace** of the monastery church of Einsiedeln.
She shows **Mary** with the infant Jesus in her arm.
She became dark from the **soot** of the candles and lamps.
Her dress is changed according to the time of the church year.
In 1798 the monks brought her to safety from French soldiers.
Pilgrims often light a candle before her.

abschnitte.text: **Einsiedeln Abbey** is a Benedictine monastery in the canton of Schwyz. It goes back to the hermit **Meinrad**, who lived there in the 9th century. In the great monastery church stands a small chapel, the **Chapel of Grace**. The Black Madonna is inside it. Einsiedeln is the most important place of pilgrimage in Switzerland and also lies on the Way of St James.

**Madonna** is another word for Mary. The wooden figure from the 15th century shows Mary carrying the infant Jesus in her arm. Mary is revered as **Queen of Heaven**, which is why she and the child wear a golden crown. The Madonna wears a splendid dress made of cloth. It is changed according to the time of the church year, and there are many different dresses.

For centuries, candles and oil lamps burned before the figure. Their **soot** gradually darkened the Madonna. When French soldiers came to Einsiedeln in 1798, the **monks** took the figure away and hid it. Later the painter **Adam Fuetscher** was to restore it. Under the soot he found the originally light colour. But because the faithful knew the Madonna as black, he painted face and hands black again. In 1803 she returned to Einsiedeln.

Since the Middle Ages, **pilgrims** have been coming to Einsiedeln. Many light a candle in front of the Chapel of Grace and say a prayer. The candle stands for a request or a thank-you. Some come on foot from far away, others in groups by bus or train.

gewusst: There are Black Madonnas at other places of pilgrimage too, for example in Altötting in Bavaria or in Częstochowa in Poland.

teile.einleitung: Metta is a word from Buddhism and means loving kindness. Buddha taught that we should be kind to all living beings, people and animals alike, even our enemies.
wichtigste: Metta means loving kindness or friendliness.
In metta meditation you wish all beings to be happy.
Karuna is the word for compassion.
The first rule for Buddhists is: do not kill or harm any living being.
Many Buddhists eat a vegetarian diet to spare animals.
According to Buddha, kindness applies to everyone, even enemies.

abschnitte.text: **Metta** comes from the ancient Indian language **Pali** and means “loving kindness” or friendliness. It means the wish that all beings are well. Metta is not only for friends and family. Buddha taught that we should be kind even to strangers and even to **enemies**. A well-known saying goes: hatred is never ended by hatred, but only by love.

In **metta meditation** you sit quietly and think kind wishes, for example: “May all beings be happy.” You often begin with yourself. Then you think of people you love, of strangers and finally of people you are quarrelling with. At the end you include **all living beings**. This is meant to make the heart kinder.

Closely linked to metta is **karuna**, compassion. Someone who has compassion wants others not to have to suffer. Metta and karuna are among the four “immeasurable” attitudes of mind in Buddhism. The other two are **sympathetic joy** and **equanimity**.

The first of the Buddhist rules is: **do not kill** or harm any living being. It applies to people and animals. That is why many Buddhists, especially many monks, eat a **vegetarian** diet. A story tells of the young Siddhartha: his cousin shot a **swan** with an arrow, and Siddhartha nursed the injured bird back to health.

gewusst: The story of the swan is often told to show that saving a life is more important than taking one.
Today metta meditation is also practised outside Buddhism, for example in courses for coping with stress.

teile.einleitung: Prayer, in Arabic salat, is one of the most important duties in Islam. Devout Muslims pray five times a day at fixed times. In doing so they follow set words and movements.
wichtigste: Devout Muslims pray **five times a day**.
Prayer is one of the five pillars of Islam.
Before praying you wash, which is the **ritual washing**.
People pray in the direction of **Mecca**.
In the prostration the **forehead** touches the ground.
On Friday there is the shared **Friday prayer** in the mosque.

abschnitte.text: The **obligatory prayer** is spread over the whole day: early in the morning before sunrise, at midday, in the afternoon, after sunset and at night. The exact times depend on the position of the sun and therefore change over the year. From the minaret the **muezzin** calls people to prayer. You can pray at home, in the mosque or in another clean place.

Before prayer you perform the **ritual washing**. For example, you wash your hands, mouth, face, arms and feet. You pray in a clean place, often on a **prayer rug**. Everyone prays in the direction of the **Kaaba** in Mecca. This direction is called the qibla. In mosques a niche in the wall, the prayer niche, shows this direction.

Prayer consists of standing, bowing, kneeling and prostrating. In the **prostration** those praying kneel and place their forehead on the ground. In this way they show humility before God. Verses from the **Quran** are spoken in Arabic. Such a sequence is repeated several times.

On Friday at midday many Muslims meet for the **Friday prayer** in the mosque. The prayer leader, the imam, gives a sermon. The believers stand next to each other in rows. In Switzerland there are numerous mosques and prayer rooms in and around the cities, often in converted buildings.

gewusst: Anyone who does not know where Mecca lies can nowadays also work out the direction of prayer with an app or a compass.
In summer in Switzerland the first and last prayers of the day lie much further apart than in winter.

teile.einleitung: “Salam aleikum” is an Arabic greeting used by Muslims all over the world. It means “peace be upon you”. There is a fixed reply to this greeting.
wichtigste: **Salam aleikum** means “peace be upon you”.
The reply is “**Wa aleikum salam**”.
This means “And upon you be peace too”.
The word **salam** means peace.
The greeting is related to the Hebrew shalom.

abschnitte.text: The full form is “As-salamu alaikum”. In everyday life people often say it more briefly, “Salam aleikum”, or simply “Salam”. Anyone greeted in this way replies with “**Wa aleikum salam**”, “And upon you be peace too”. The greeting is used on arriving and sometimes on leaving too. It is spoken not only among friends but also among strangers.

The Arabic word **salam** means peace. The word **Islam** has the same word root too. With the greeting you wish the other person peace and well-being. In Islam it counts as a good deed to greet others in this way and to return the greeting kindly.

Arabic and **Hebrew** are related languages. That is why “Salam aleikum” resembles the Hebrew “Shalom aleichem”, which also means “peace be upon you”. Christianity also has a similar wish: in the service people say “Peace be with you”. The greeting is also widespread in many countries where Arabic is not spoken, for example in Turkey, in Iran or in the Balkans.

gewusst: Even people who do not speak Arabic know this greeting, because it is used throughout the Islamic world.

teile.einleitung: New Atheism is a current of criticism of religion that became well known around 2006. Its representatives say that there is no God, and criticise religion openly. They rely above all on natural science and reason.
wichtigste: The main representatives are regarded as Richard Dawkins, Daniel Dennett, Sam Harris and Christopher Hitchens.
The four are also called “the Four Horsemen”.
Sam Harris’s book “The End of Faith” from 2004 is often seen as the beginning.
Dawkins’s book “The God Delusion” from 2006 became a bestseller.
The journalist Gary Wolf coined the term “New Atheism” in 2006.
Unlike older atheism, New Atheism takes an offensive stance.

abschnitte.text: **Atheism** means not believing in a god. That has existed for a long time. But **New Atheism** is especially **offensive** in its stance. Its representatives think that religion should not just be tolerated but openly **criticised**. They draw their arguments mainly from biology, physics and philosophy. The term **“New Atheism”** was coined by the journalist **Gary Wolf** in 2006 in the magazine “Wired”.

The beginning is often seen as the book **“The End of Faith”** by **Sam Harris** from 2004. He wrote it under the impression of the attacks of 11 September 2001. In 2006 **“The God Delusion”** by **Richard Dawkins** appeared. In the same year the philosopher **Daniel Dennett** published “Breaking the Spell”. In 2007 **“God Is Not Great”** by **Christopher Hitchens** followed.

Dawkins, Dennett, Harris and Hitchens met in 2007 for a filmed conversation. It became known under the name **“The Four Horsemen”**. The name alludes to the four horsemen of the Apocalypse in the Bible. Dawkins is a biologist, Dennett was a philosopher, Harris is a neuroscientist and Hitchens was a journalist. Dennett examined religion as a **natural phenomenon** that could be explained through evolution and culture.

New Atheism set off many **discussions**. Supporters praise it for asking clear questions and stressing science. Critics, including some atheists, find the tone too **sharp** and the view of religion too one-sided. Philosophers and theologians who believe wrote books in reply. The debate shows how differently people think about belief and knowledge.

gewusst: In 1976 Dawkins also coined the word “meme” for ideas that spread from person to person like genes.
Christopher Hitchens died in 2011, Daniel Dennett in 2024.

teile.einleitung: In Hinduism, purushartha means “aim of a human being”. The teaching describes four aims of life that together are meant to make a good and meaningful life.
wichtigste: The classical teaching knows four aims of life: dharma, artha, kama and moksha.
Dharma is the right order and limits the other aims.
Artha means prosperity and material success.
Kama means joy, pleasure and a sense of beauty.
Moksha is the highest aim, liberation from the cycle of births.
Wealth and joy are regarded as legitimate as long as they stay within the framework of dharma.

abschnitte.text: The teaching of the **purusharthas** names four aims: **dharma**, **artha**, **kama** and **moksha**. In earlier times people often spoke of only the first three. Moksha was added later as the fourth and highest aim. The aims are not meant to oppose one another, but to complement each other.

**Dharma** means the right order, duty and right action. It forms the framework for all the other aims. Prosperity and joy are good only if they agree with this order. Someone who becomes rich by cheating others, for example, violates dharma.

**Artha** includes property, work and political success. In Hinduism it is regarded as a legitimate aim, because people need money to provide for a family. The ancient Indian textbook **Arthashastra** belongs to artha. It is attributed to **Kautilya**, also called Chanakya, an adviser to King Chandragupta. It deals with administration, taxes and diplomacy.

**Kama** refers to desires and the enjoyment of pleasant things. This includes, for example, **art**, **music** and good food. This aim too is meant to be limited by dharma. So Hinduism does not reject joy, but wants people to enjoy it in moderation.

The first three aims concern life in the world. **Moksha** leads beyond it. It means liberation from the cycle of birth, death and rebirth. According to the classical teaching, different aims suit different **stages of life**: in old age moksha moves more and more into the foreground.

gewusst: The Arthashastra is one of the oldest books in the world on statecraft and economics.
The word “dharma” is also used in Buddhism and Jainism, but there with a somewhat different meaning.

teile.einleitung: The lotus flower is a beautiful water plant from Asia. It grows out of the mud and yet blooms perfectly clean. That is why in Hinduism and Buddhism it is a sign of purity.
wichtigste: The lotus flower grows in ponds and lakes.
Its roots are in the mud at the bottom.
It is a sign of purity.
Water beads off its leaves and takes the dirt with it.
It is regarded as the national flower of India.
The blossoms are often pink or white.

abschnitte.text: The lotus flower grows **in the water**, in ponds and lakes. Its **roots** are in the **mud** at the bottom. The large round **leaves** float on the water or stand up above it. The blossom stands high above the water. Lotus blossoms are often **pink** or white, some white with pink tips.

On a lotus leaf, drops of water simply roll off. As they do so they take the **dirt** with them. This is because of tiny bumps and a waxy layer on the leaf. Researchers call this the **lotus effect**. Today it is used for paints, glass and fabrics that almost clean themselves.

The lotus grows out of the mud and yet blooms perfectly clean. That is why it stands for **purity**. In **Hinduism** and **Buddhism** it is a holy sign. In pictures the god **Vishnu** almost always holds a **lotus blossom** in one of his four hands. In many pictures Buddha too sits on a lotus blossom.

The lotus flower is regarded as the **national flower of India**. It can be seen there on many pictures and buildings. In Asia, parts of the plant are eaten too. The thick **root** is boiled or fried, and the **seeds** can be eaten as well. The lotus flower is not the same as the **water lily**, which you can also see in Swiss ponds.

gewusst: Lotus seeds stay able to sprout for a very long time, and some have sprouted even after several hundred years.
The lotus flower can keep its blossom somewhat warmer than its surroundings.

teile.einleitung: In Roman religion, Mars was the god of war. He was one of the most important gods of Rome, and to this day a month and a planet bear his name.
wichtigste: Mars was the Roman god of war.
He corresponded to the Greek god Ares.
The month of March is named after him.
The reddish planet Mars also bears his name.
According to legend, Romulus and Remus were his sons.
A she-wolf is said to have suckled the twins, and the wolf was the animal of Mars.

abschnitte.text: **Mars** was the god of war. **Soldiers** in particular worshipped him and asked him for protection and victory. He was usually shown with a helmet, shield and spear. Originally he was probably also a protector of fields and cattle. His animal was the **wolf**, his bird the woodpecker.

Many Roman gods correspond to Greek gods. The Greek god of war was called **Ares**. Among the Greeks, Ares was not very popular, because he stood for the wild side of war. The Romans, by contrast, worshipped Mars greatly. They saw him as a protector of their people.

According to legend, the twins **Romulus** and **Remus** were sons of Mars. As babies they were abandoned. A **she-wolf** found them and gave them milk. Later they were brought up by a shepherd. Romulus is then said to have founded the city of **Rome**. That is why the Romans saw themselves as descendants of Mars.

**March** is called “Martius” in Latin, that is, the month of Mars. In the early Roman calendar the year began with March. Military campaigns also began in spring. In some languages Tuesday too is named after Mars, for example “mardi” in French.

The planet **Mars** shines reddish in the night sky. This colour reminded people of blood and war. That is why it was given the name of the god of war. Its two small moons are called **Phobos** and **Deimos**, which mean “fear” and “terror”.

gewusst: The Campus Martius, in English the Field of Mars, was a large open space in Rome where soldiers trained.
The red colour of the planet Mars comes from iron oxide, that is, rust, in the dust.

teile.einleitung: Church bells hang high up in the church tower. Their sound calls people to worship, tells the time and accompanies special moments in the life of a village. In Switzerland you can hear them in almost every municipality.
wichtigste: Church bells hang in the church tower so that they can be heard far away.
They are mostly made of bell metal, a mixture of copper and tin.
On Saturday evening they ring in Sunday.
In many villages the midday bell rings at 11 or 12 o’clock.
A single, slowly tolling bell often announces a death.
On New Year’s Eve the bells ring in the new year.

abschnitte.text: Church bells hang high up in the **church tower**. This way they can be heard across the whole village. Most are made of **bell metal**, a mixture of copper and tin. Inside hangs a heavy **clapper**, which strikes the rim as the bell swings. Large bells sound deep, small ones high. Today many bells are driven electrically.

abschnitte.titel: Bells in the course of the day
abschnitte.text: In the past people had no watches. The bells told them the **time**. In many villages the midday bell rings at **11 or 12 o’clock**. For the farmers that meant: time to eat. On Saturday evening the bells ring for longer. People say they **ring in Sunday**.

Bells also accompany sad and happy events. If a **single bell** tolls slowly, often someone has died. This **death knell** tells the village of a person’s death. At weddings and christenings, by contrast, the bells ring merrily. On **New Year’s Eve**, at midnight, all the bells ring in many places and welcome the new year.

From Maundy Thursday to the Easter Vigil the bells in Catholic churches **fall silent**. In some regions children are told that the bells have **flown to Rome**. On the night of Easter they return and ring again. During the quiet days, wooden rattles are used in many places instead of bells.

Old bells often carry inscriptions. On a bell of the Minster in **Schaffhausen** it says in Latin: “I call the living, I mourn the dead, I break the lightning”. This inscription inspired the poet **Friedrich Schiller** to write his famous poem “The Song of the Bell”. The old bell can still be seen in Schaffhausen today.

gewusst: Children are told that the church bells fly to Rome before Easter.
A bell in Schaffhausen inspired Friedrich Schiller to write “The Song of the Bell”.

teile.einleitung: The Maya in Central America developed an ingenious calendar system. They linked several calendars together and so could calculate very long periods of time precisely.
wichtigste: The sacred ritual calendar, the Tzolk’in, has 260 days.
The solar year, the Haab, has 18 months of 20 days and 5 extra days, so 365 days.
After 52 years the Calendar Round begins again from the start.
The Maya counted in a base-20 system.
They had a sign for zero from early on.
On 21 December 2012 a great period of the Long Count came to an end.

abschnitte.text: The **Maya** counted in a **base-20 system**, probably using fingers and toes. For their numbers they needed only three signs: a **dot** stood for 1, a **bar** for 5 and a shell for **zero**. The Maya knew zero long before the Europeans. In Europe it only caught on in the Middle Ages, through Arab scholars.

The **Tzolk’in** was the sacred ritual calendar. It combines 13 numbers with 20 day names, and 13 times 20 makes **260 days**. Alongside it there was the solar year, the **Haab**. It consisted of **18 months of 20 days**, so 360 days, plus 5 extra days. So the Haab had **365 days**, almost as many as our year.

The Maya ran both calendars at the same time, like two interlocking cogwheels. A particular combination of a Tzolk’in day and a Haab day only comes round again after **18,980 days**. That is **52 years**. This period is called the **Calendar Round**. For even longer periods the Maya used the **Long Count**, which counted the days since a starting date in the distant past.

On **21 December 2012** a great period of the Long Count came to an end. Some people claimed that the Maya had predicted the **end of the world** for this day. That is not true. For the Maya, the end of a cycle was more of a new beginning, just as a new century begins for us. Of course the world did not end either.

gewusst: A Maya who reached the age of 52 lived to see the end of a whole Calendar Round, which was regarded as a special event.
Even today some Maya communities in Guatemala still use the 260-day calendar.

teile.einleitung: The ancient Olympic Games were great sporting contests in ancient Greece. They took place every four years in Olympia, in honour of the god Zeus. They were also a religious festival.
wichtigste: The first surviving list of winners dates from 776 BC.
The Games took place in Olympia in honour of Zeus.
The four-year period between two Games was called an Olympiad.
The oldest contest was the stadion race of just under 200 metres.
Winners received a wreath from the sacred olive tree.
A sacred truce, the ekecheiria, protected journeys to Olympia.
Phidias made the huge statue of Zeus in the temple.

abschnitte.text: The Games took place in **Olympia**, a sanctuary in the west of the Peloponnese peninsula. They honoured the father of the gods, **Zeus**. Besides the contests there were sacrifices and prayers. In the temple stood a huge **statue of Zeus** made of gold and ivory. The sculptor **Phidias** had made it. It was about 12 metres high and was one of the **Seven Wonders** of the ancient world.

According to tradition, the **lists of winners** begin in the year **776 BC**. The Games took place every four years. The period between two Games was called an **Olympiad**. The Greeks even counted their years in Olympiads. Today the word is often used for the Games themselves. Strictly speaking, though, it means the span of time in between.

The oldest contest was the **stadion race**. It ran over one length of the stadium, in Olympia just under **200 metres**. For a long time it was the only contest. Later further races, wrestling, boxing, **chariot racing** and the **pentathlon** were added. The athletes mostly competed without clothes. Winners received an **olive wreath**, cut from a sacred olive tree. At home they often received further honours.

For the time of the Games the **ekecheiria** applied, a sacred **truce**. Athletes and spectators were supposed to be able to travel safely to Olympia. This was important, because the Greek cities often made war on one another. Today’s Olympic Games take up this idea again with the **Olympic Truce**.

In honour of the goddess **Hera**, Olympia also had its own races for **girls** and young women. They were called the **Heraia** and took place in three age groups. The winners received a wreath. The ancient Olympic Games ended at the end of the 4th century AD. Only in **1896** did modern Olympic Games take place again, in Athens. The International Olympic Committee is today based in **Lausanne**.

gewusst: The Olympic flame for the modern Games is still lit in Olympia today with a concave mirror and sunlight.
In Lausanne there is the Olympic Museum, which also shows the ancient Games.

teile.einleitung: Purim is a joyful Jewish festival. It recalls Queen Esther, who saved her people from an evil plot. Children and adults dress up and celebrate noisily.
wichtigste: At Purim children and adults dress up.
The heroine of the story is Queen Esther.
The villain is called Haman.
Whenever the name Haman is read out, everyone makes a noise.
The pastry for Purim is called hamantaschen and is triangular.
People give each other food and sweets and also give gifts to the poor.
The story is set in Persia, present-day Iran.

abschnitte.text: The story is in the **Book of Esther** in the Bible. It is set at the court of the king of **Persia**. The powerful minister **Haman** wanted to harm all the Jews in the country. The Jewish queen **Esther** and her relative **Mordecai** found out about it. Esther bravely went to the king and was able to prevent the plan.

At Purim the whole story of Esther is read out from a scroll in the synagogue. Whenever the name **Haman** is mentioned, everyone makes a **noise**. The children spin rattles, clap and stamp. In this way the name of the villain is drowned out.

At Purim many people put on **costumes**. There are games, plays and processions. This is a little like the **carnival** in Switzerland. Both festivals are fun and noisy. Purim is usually in February or March.

The typical pastry is called **hamantaschen**. They are triangular pockets of dough, often filled with poppy seed, jam or chocolate. At Purim people bring friends and neighbours small packages of **food and sweets**. Gifts are also given to poor people, so that everyone can join in the celebration.

gewusst: In the Book of Esther the word “God” does not appear even once.
The name Purim means “lots”, because in the story Haman chose a day by drawing lots.

teile.einleitung: The Festival of Sacrifice is the highest festival in Islam. Muslims celebrate it at the time of the pilgrimage to Mecca. It recalls Abraham, who trusted God completely.
wichtigste: The Festival of Sacrifice is called Eid al-Adha in Arabic and Kurban Bayramı in Turkish.
It is the highest festival in Islam.
It falls at the time of the Hajj pilgrimage to Mecca.
It recalls Abraham, who was ready to sacrifice his son to God.
God sent a ram instead.
Many families share meat with relatives and people in need.

abschnitte.titel: A festival at the time of the pilgrimage
abschnitte.text: The **Festival of Sacrifice** is called **Eid al-Adha** in Arabic and **Kurban Bayramı** in Turkish. It is the highest festival in **Islam**. It takes place at the time of the **Hajj**, the great pilgrimage to **Mecca**. Because the Islamic calendar follows the moon, the festival falls about 11 days earlier every year. It usually lasts four days.

The festival recalls **Abraham**, called **Ibrahim** in Islam. According to tradition, God demanded of him that he sacrifice his son. Abraham trusted God and was ready to do it. But God held him back and sent a **ram**, which was sacrificed in place of the son. The story shows Abraham’s great **trust in God**. Jews and Christians also know a similar story.

In the morning many Muslims attend a **festival prayer** at the mosque. Afterwards an animal, such as a sheep, is traditionally slaughtered. The meat is often **shared**: one part for the family, one part for relatives and friends and one part for **people in need**. Families visit one another, and children get presents. In **Switzerland**, slaughter without stunning is forbidden. Many families therefore buy meat or give money for people in need.

gewusst: The Festival of Sacrifice lasts longer than the festival at the end of the fasting month of Ramadan.
Many Muslims give money at the Festival of Sacrifice so that poor families in other countries can receive meat.

teile.einleitung: Laozi is a famous Chinese sage who is regarded as the founder of Daoism. Almost nothing certain is known about his life, and there are mostly legends. The book Daodejing is ascribed to him, one of the best-known books of China.
wichtigste: Laozi means roughly “old master”.
He is said to have lived in the 6th century BC.
According to the legend he left China on a water buffalo.
A border guard asked him to write down his teaching.
He is said to have been an archivist at the court of the Zhou kings.
In religious Daoism Laozi is worshipped as a deity.

abschnitte.text: “Lao” means **old**, and “zi” is an honorary title for a **master** or teacher. Laozi is therefore more of an **honorary name** than a real personal name. Tradition makes him an older contemporary of **Confucius** in the **6th century BC**. Some experts, however, date the texts ascribed to him later.

The historian **Sima Qian** reports that Laozi was an **archivist** at the royal court of the **Zhou**. So he looked after important writings. Old texts also tell of a meeting with the younger **Confucius**. Whether this meeting really took place is not known.

The best-known **legend** tells how the aged Laozi left China on a **water buffalo**, heading west. At the border pass the guard **Yin Xi** asked him to write down his wisdom. This is how the book **Daodejing** is said to have come into being. After that Laozi travelled on, and nobody saw him again. That is why many Chinese pictures show him on a buffalo.

At the centre stands the **Dao**, the “Way”. This means a force that orders everything in the world. Human beings should live in harmony with nature and not fight against it. An important idea is **wu wei**, acting without force. Water is regarded as the model: it is soft and yields, yet in time hollows out even stones.

In religious **Daoism** Laozi was made divine. He is worshipped under the name **Taishang Laojun**. In Daoist temples there are therefore figures of him. Because there is hardly any reliable information about him, some experts think he is an **invented** figure or one put together from several people.

gewusst: The Daodejing is very short, with only about 5,000 characters.
The Daodejing is among the books that have been translated most often into other languages.

teile.einleitung: Shankara, also called Adi Shankara, was an Indian philosopher and teacher. He is regarded as the most important representative of Advaita Vedanta, a teaching of Hinduism. According to the usual dating, he lived in the 8th century.
wichtigste: According to the usual dating, Shankara lived in the 8th century AD.
Tradition names Kaladi in present-day Kerala as his birthplace.
He taught that the soul and the divine are at bottom one.
He wrote commentaries on the three basic texts of Vedanta.
According to tradition, he founded monasteries in the four directions of India.

abschnitte.text: Little is known for certain about Shankara’s life, and much comes from legends. Tradition names **Kaladi** in present-day **Kerala** in southern India as his birthplace. He is said to have become an ascetic while still young, that is, a person who gives up possessions. He wandered through all of India and debated with scholars. He died young but left behind great works of commentary.

**Advaita** means “non-duality”. Shankara taught that the inner self, the **atman**, and the divine, the **Brahman**, are ultimately the same. The world of many things is like a veil, called **maya**. According to this teaching, anyone who recognises the true unity is freed from the cycle of rebirths.

Shankara wrote commentaries on the **Upanishads**, the **Bhagavad Gita** and the **Brahma Sutras**. These three basic texts are together called the **Prasthanatraya**. According to tradition, he founded monasteries, so-called **mathas**, in the four directions of India. Named are Sringeri, Dvaraka, Puri and Jyotirmath. Their heads still bear the title **Shankaracharya** today.

gewusst: The monasteries founded by Shankara are said, according to tradition, to have been run for over a thousand years.

teile.einleitung: Confucius was a Chinese teacher and thinker who lived about 2,500 years ago. His teaching, Confucianism, shaped China and other countries of East Asia for many centuries. It is mainly about good behaviour, respect and a just order.
wichtigste: Confucius was born in 551 BC in the state of Lu.
He became famous above all as a teacher.
His sayings are in the texts called the “Analects”.
Ren means humaneness, Xiao respect for parents.
Under the Han dynasty Confucianism became the state doctrine.
For a long time, officials had to know the Confucian classics for examinations.

abschnitte.text: Confucius was born in **551 BC** in the small **state of Lu**. This lay in what is now Shandong province, and his home town is the city of **Qufu**. His Chinese name is Kong Fuzi, which means “Master Kong”. In his time China was divided into many states, which often fought each other. Confucius looked for a path to peace and good order. He died in 479 BC.

Confucius became famous as a **teacher**. According to tradition he had about 3,000 pupils. He wanted not only nobles but all gifted people to be able to learn. His pupils and their pupils collected his sayings. This collection is called the **“Analects”**, in Chinese **Lunyu**.

A **virtue** is a good quality. For Confucius the highest virtue was **Ren**, humaneness or kindness towards others. Also very important is **Xiao**, respect for parents: children should honour their parents and look after them in old age. Then there is **Li**, correct behaviour and rites. A person who lives this way is regarded as a **noble person**.

Confucius saw society as a web of relationships. The **five relationships** are: ruler and subject, father and son, husband and wife, older and younger brother, and friend and friend. In every relationship each side has **duties**. When everyone fulfils their duties, then according to this teaching there is harmony.

Under Emperor Wu of the **Han dynasty**, Confucianism became the **state doctrine** in the 2nd century BC. Whoever wanted to become an official had to know and interpret the Confucian classics in difficult **state examinations**. These examinations were not abolished until **1905**. In Korea, Japan and Vietnam too, the teaching has left its mark.

gewusst: The name “Confucius” is a Latin form that European missionaries made from Kong Fuzi.
The temple, cemetery and family home of Confucius in Qufu are a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

teile.einleitung: Shamans are found among many peoples of the world, especially in Siberia, in the far north and in America. They are regarded as healers and as people who can make contact with spirits. Their most important tool is often the drum.
wichtigste: A **shaman** is regarded among his people as a healer and expert in spirits.
The word comes from the language of the **Evenks** in Siberia.
The most important instrument is the **frame drum**.
Its skin is animal hide, in the north often reindeer hide.
According to the belief, helper spirits often appear as animals.
Among the Sami the shaman was called a **noaidi**.

abschnitte.text: A **shaman** is an important person among many peoples. It is believed that they can speak with spirits and in this way heal the sick, give advice or influence the weather. To do so they put themselves into a special state, **trance**. According to the belief, their soul then travels into the spirit world. This form of belief is called **shamanism**.

The word “shaman” comes from the Tungusic language of the **Evenks**, a people in Siberia. Through Russian it passed into other languages. Later it was also used for similar healers all over the world. Among the **Sami** in Lapland in the north of Europe, the shaman was called a **noaidi**.

The most important instrument is the **frame drum**. An animal hide is stretched over a round wooden frame, in the north often a **reindeer hide**. The drum is held in one hand and struck with a beater in a steady rhythm. This is meant to help in reaching trance. The drum is often regarded as a steed on which the shaman travels into the spirit world. On many drums animals, sun, moon and spirits are painted.

Many shamans believe in **helper spirits** that accompany and protect them. These often appear as animals, for example as a bear, a bird or a wolf. The pictures on the drums show how the people imagined the world with its various levels. Many of these drums can be seen in museums today.

gewusst: Many Sami drums were collected or burned by missionaries in the past, which is why only a few survive.
Women too can be shamans, among some peoples even especially often.

teile.einleitung: Moksha is a central concept in Hinduism. It means liberation from the cycle of birth, death and rebirth and is seen as the highest goal of life.
wichtigste: Moksha means liberation from the cycle of rebirths.
Someone who is already liberated during their lifetime is called a Jivanmukta.
The final liberation at the death of the body is called Videhamukti.
According to Advaita Vedanta, the realisation of the unity of Atman and Brahman brings liberation.
Many Bhakti schools see liberation as eternal loving fellowship with God.
The stage of life called Sannyasa is devoted entirely to the pursuit of Moksha.
Varanasi on the Ganges is seen by many as a place where dying grants Moksha.

abschnitte.text: According to Hindu belief, the soul is born anew again and again after death. This cycle is called **Samsara**. What you do has consequences for the next life, which is called **karma**. **Moksha** is liberation from this cycle. Anyone who reaches it is not reborn any more. Moksha is regarded as the highest of the four aims of life in Hinduism.

The schools of Hinduism describe the path in different ways. According to **Advaita Vedanta** and its teacher **Shankara**, bondage arises from ignorance. Only **knowledge**, in Sanskrit Jnana, that one’s own self, the **Atman**, is one with **Brahman**, the highest reality, brings liberation. Many **Bhakti schools**, for example that of **Ramanuja**, see it differently. For them the soul remains distinct from God even in liberation and lives in eternal, loving fellowship with him.

Some teachings say that a person can reach Moksha during their lifetime. Such a person is called a **Jivanmukta**, “liberated in life”. They go on living, but inwardly are no longer bound by karma. When their body dies, the final liberation follows. It is called **Videhamukti**, “liberation without a body”.

The traditional order divides life into four stages. The last is called **Sannyasa**, life as a renunciant. A **Sannyasin** gives up possessions and family. He often wanders from place to place and devotes himself entirely to the search for liberation. Today only a few people choose this path.

The city of **Varanasi**, also called Kashi, lies on the holy river **Ganges**. It is regarded as the city of the god **Shiva**. Many Hindus believe that anyone who dies in Varanasi reaches Moksha. That is why old people come there, and many of the dead are cremated at the **ghats**, the steps on the river bank.

gewusst: Varanasi is one of the oldest continuously inhabited cities in the world.
In Buddhism and Jainism too there is the idea of liberation from the cycle of rebirths.

teile.einleitung: St Martin’s Day is on 11 November. On this day people remember Saint Martin, who shared his cloak with a freezing beggar. In many places children walk through the streets with lanterns.
wichtigste: St Martin’s Day is on 11 November.
It commemorates Saint Martin of Tours.
According to legend, Martin shared his cloak with a beggar.
At the Martin’s procession children carry lanterns and sing songs.
In Switzerland, Sursee in the canton of Lucerne is known for the “Gansabhauet”.

abschnitte.text: **Martin** lived in the 4th century and was at first a Roman soldier. According to the legend, he rode past a freezing **beggar** on a cold winter’s day. He had nothing with him except his cloak. So he cut it in two with his sword and gave half to the beggar. Later Martin became a Christian and eventually **Bishop of Tours** in France.

On St Martin’s Day children walk through the streets with **lanterns**. They often make the lanterns themselves at school or nursery. They sing songs such as “Ich geh mit meiner Laterne” (“I walk with my lantern”). The light is meant to remind us that Martin did good and so brought light into the world.

A legend tells that Martin did not want to become a bishop and hid in a **goose pen**. The cackling geese gave him away. That is why in some areas people eat a **Martin’s goose** on St Martin’s Day. In the past 11 November was also a day for paying dues: farmers paid their taxes, often with geese.

In Switzerland, lantern processions are common above all in Catholic areas. In **Sursee** in the canton of Lucerne the **Gansabhauet** takes place on St Martin’s Day. Blindfolded participants try to strike down a dead goose hanging up with a blunt sabre. They wear a golden sun mask while doing so.

gewusst: Many churches in Europe are called St Martin’s Church, because Martin is one of the most popular saints.
In many areas the carnival season begins on 11 November, St Martin’s Day.

teile.einleitung: Niklaus von Flüe, known as Brother Klaus, is the best-known saint of Switzerland. He was a farmer and father of a family and later lived as a hermit in the Ranft in Obwalden. He is regarded as a peacemaker and patron saint of Switzerland.
wichtigste: Niklaus von Flüe lived in the 15th century, from 1417 to 1487.
He came from Flüeli in what is now the canton of Obwalden.
He was a farmer, a councillor and the father of ten children.
At about the age of 50 he became a hermit in the Ranft gorge.
In 1481 his advice helped the Confederates to reach agreement in Stans.
Pope Pius XII declared him a saint in 1947.
He is regarded as the patron saint of Switzerland.

abschnitte.text: Niklaus von Flüe was born in **1417** in **Flüeli** in what is now the canton of **Obwalden**. He ran a **farm** and married Dorothea Wyss. The two had **ten children**. Niklaus was respected, took part in military campaigns and was a **councillor** and judge. But he felt more and more strongly the wish to live entirely for God.

At about the age of 50, in 1467, Niklaus left his family with his wife’s consent. He became a **hermit** in the **Ranft gorge**, very close to his farm. There he lived in a small **cell** next to a chapel. He prayed a great deal and received people who were seeking advice. From then on he was called **Brother Klaus**.

It is told of Brother Klaus that for about **20 years** he **ate almost nothing**. People of his time were amazed by this and even put it to the test. Many saw it as a miracle. It cannot be proved today. But the story made Brother Klaus widely known even in his lifetime.

In **1481** the member states of the **Confederation** quarrelled fiercely, among other things over the admission of Fribourg and Solothurn. A civil war threatened. The parish priest of Stans sought advice from Brother Klaus in the Ranft. Afterwards the states agreed in the **Stanser Verkommnis** (Covenant of Stans). Fribourg and Solothurn were admitted to the Confederation. That is why Brother Klaus is regarded as a **peacemaker**.

Brother Klaus died in **1487**. Soon many people venerated him. In **1947** **Pope Pius XII** declared him a saint. He is regarded as the **patron saint** of Switzerland, that is, the protector of the whole country. His feast day in Switzerland is **25 September**. Many people still make a pilgrimage to Flüeli and the Ranft today.

gewusst: Brother Klaus is also respected as a peacemaker by many Reformed people in Switzerland.
His prayer is well known: “My Lord and my God, take from me everything that keeps me from you.”

teile.einleitung: Li is an important concept in Confucianism. It means rites and custom, that is, the right forms of behaviour. For Confucius these rules brought order into people’s life together.
wichtigste: Li means rites, custom and correct behaviour.
It includes rituals, politeness and rules of good manners.
For Confucius, Li and Ren, humaneness, belong together.
Xunzi stressed the rites especially strongly.
The Book of Rites is one of the Five Classics.

abschnitte.text: The Chinese character **礼** is pronounced “Li”. It means **rites** and **custom**. What is meant are rituals at festivals, but also **forms of politeness** in everyday life, for example how you greet parents, teachers or guests. These rules give life together an **order**. Everyone knows how to behave towards others.

In the **Analects** of Confucius, the **Lunyu**, a pupil asks about humaneness, **Ren**. Confucius answers in section 12.1: to overcome oneself and return to the rites, that is Ren. Someone who controls themselves and respects custom therefore acts humanely. **Ren** and **Li** thus belong closely together. Outer form and inner attitude should agree.

Later Confucians thought differently about human beings. **Mengzi** believed that human beings have a good disposition. **Xunzi**, by contrast, held that human nature is bad. That is why he stressed the **rites** especially: through **education** and Li, he said, a person is shaped towards the good.

Among the **Five Classics** of Confucianism is the **Book of Rites**, in Chinese **Liji**. It describes ceremonies, mourning customs and rules of good manners. Two of its chapters were later read as books in their own right. They are called “The Great Learning” and “The Doctrine of the Mean” and belong to the **Four Books** of Confucianism.

gewusst: In China, Korea and Japan, Confucian rules of politeness still shape how older people are greeted.
In the past the rites also included the right music at ceremonies.

teile.einleitung: Freedom of religion means that every person may decide for themselves what they believe. In Switzerland this right is protected in the Federal Constitution. It applies to everyone who lives here.
wichtigste: Freedom of religion is in **Article 15** of the Federal Constitution.
There it is called **freedom of belief and conscience**.
No one may be forced to join a religion.
You may freely choose your religion, change it or leave it.
From the age of 16, young people decide about their religion themselves.
The Universal Declaration of Human Rights of 1948 also protects freedom of religion.

abschnitte.text: Article 15 of the **Federal Constitution** guarantees freedom of belief and conscience. The **conscience** is the inner voice that tells you what is right. Every person may freely choose their religion and profess it alone or together with others. That is why there are services, prayers and religious festivals. No one may be forced to join a religious community, to belong to one or to take part in religious acts.

Freedom of religion also includes the right to **change** your religion or to have none at all. Anyone who no longer wants to be a member of their church can declare that they are **leaving the church**. In Switzerland a written declaration to the parish is usually enough. Under the **Civil Code**, young people from the age of 16 decide for themselves about their religious profession. Before that, their parents decide.

In 1948 the **UN** adopted the Universal Declaration of Human Rights. Article 18 contains freedom of thought, conscience and religion. It applies to all people in the world. The European Convention on Human Rights, which Switzerland has joined, also protects this right.

Freedom of religion did not always apply to everyone equally. After the **Sonderbund War**, the Federal Constitution of 1848 banned the Catholic order of the **Jesuits**. Only in 1973 did the voters lift this ban. Even today people sometimes discuss where freedom of religion has limits, for example when it clashes with other rights or rules. Then the courts and politicians have to weigh things up.

gewusst: Freedom of religion also protects people who believe in no god at all.
At 16 you cannot yet vote in Switzerland, but you can already decide about your religion yourself.

teile.einleitung: The Mishnah is an important collection of Jewish religious law. It was completed around the year 200 AD and forms the basis of the Talmud.
wichtigste: The Mishnah collects teachings that had previously been passed on by word of mouth.
It is divided into six orders, the Sedarim, with 63 tractates in all.
According to tradition, Rabbi Judah the Prince was its editor.
The scholars whose opinions it collects are called Tannaim.
The first tractate is called Berakhot and deals with blessings and prayers.
The tractate Pirkei Avot contains the “Sayings of the Fathers”.

abschnitte.text: Alongside the written **Torah**, Judaism had many teachings that were passed on by word of mouth. They explained how to follow the commandments in everyday life. The scholars who discussed these teachings are called **Tannaim**. They were active until about 200 AD. So that the teachings would not be lost, they were eventually collected and written down.

According to tradition, **Rabbi Judah the Prince** (Judah ha-Nasi) arranged the oral teachings and completed the collection. He was the **Patriarch**, that is, the head of the Jews in Palestine. The Mishnah also quotes older scholars, for example **Hillel** and **Akiva**. Often different opinions stand side by side.

The Mishnah is divided into **six orders**, in Hebrew **Sedarim**. Together they contain **63 tractates**, that is, sections on particular subjects. That is why the Talmud is also called **“Shas”**, an abbreviation for “six orders”. The first order is called **Zeraim** and begins with the tractate **Berakhot** on blessings and prayers. It first asks from when in the evening one may say the Shema Yisrael.

A special tractate is **Pirkei Avot**, the “Sayings of the Fathers”. It contains no laws, but **words of wisdom for life** from the rabbis. Hillel’s saying is famous: “If I am not for myself, who will be for me?” The tractate is traditionally read on the Sabbaths in summer.

gewusst: Together with the later explanations, the Gemara, the Mishnah forms the Talmud.
The word Mishnah comes from a Hebrew word meaning “to repeat”, because people learned by repeating.

teile.einleitung: St Peter’s Basilica is one of the largest churches in the world. It stands in Vatican City in the middle of Rome and is the most important place of worship of the Catholic Church.
wichtigste: St Peter’s Basilica stands in Vatican City in Rome.
It is one of the largest churches in the world.
It was built over the tomb of the apostle Peter.
The huge dome was built to plans by Michelangelo.
The Pope celebrates important services here.
The Swiss Guard protects the Pope and the Vatican.

abschnitte.text: According to tradition, the apostle **Peter** was buried in Rome. Over his tomb Emperor Constantine built a first church in the 4th century. Because it grew old and dilapidated, work on the present St Peter’s began in **1506**. It was consecrated only over 100 years later, in 1626.

Many famous artists worked on St Peter’s. **Bramante** drew up the first plans. **Michelangelo** planned the enormous **dome**, which can be seen from far away. Later **Bernini** designed St Peter’s Square with its great colonnades. Inside, above the altar, stands a huge canopy made of bronze.

St Peter’s contains many works of art. Especially well known is the **Pietà** by Michelangelo. It shows Mary holding her dead son Jesus on her lap. Beneath the basilica lie the tombs of many popes. Every year millions of people visit the church.

The Pope is protected by the **Pontifical Swiss Guard**. It has existed since 1506, the year in which the building of St Peter’s began. All the guards are young Catholic men with Swiss citizenship. Their colourful uniforms in blue, yellow and red are famous the world over.

gewusst: Vatican City, in which St Peter’s stands, is the smallest state in the world.
You can climb up the dome of St Peter’s and look out over the whole of Rome.

teile.einleitung: The Parsis are a small religious community in India. They follow the old religion of Zarathustra, Zoroastrianism, and originally come from Persia, present-day Iran.
wichtigste: The Parsis are Zoroastrians in India, and their name means “Persians”.
Their ancestors left Persia after the Islamic conquest because of pressure and persecution.
The largest community lives today in Mumbai.
The business family Tata and the singer Freddie Mercury come from Parsi families.
At the Navjote a child receives a white shirt and a sacred cord.
Traditionally Parsis lay their dead on the Towers of Silence.

abschnitte.text: In the 7th century Arab Muslim armies conquered **Persia**. After that the **Zoroastrians** there came under increasing pressure. Some of them fled across the sea to western India, to the region of **Gujarat**. Their descendants are called **Parsis**, which means “Persians”. They worship the god **Ahura Mazda**, proclaimed by the prophet Zarathustra.

In the temples of the Parsis a sacred **fire** burns, which must never go out. For them the fire is a sign of purity and of God’s light. The Parsis do not worship the fire, but pray in front of it. Some temples may be entered only by Parsis.

Most Parsis live in **Mumbai**, formerly Bombay. They have strongly shaped the city through trade and industry. In the 19th century **Jamsetji Tata** founded the **Tata Group**, today one of the largest companies in India. **Freddie Mercury**, the singer of the band Queen, also had Parsi parents. His real name was Farrokh Bulsara and he was born in Zanzibar in 1946.

At the ceremony called **Navjote**, a child is admitted to the community. The child receives the white shirt **sudreh** and the sacred cord **kusti**. The cord is tied several times around the body and retied during prayer. For the family the ceremony is a big celebration.

According to Parsi belief, the dead should not pollute either earth or fire. That is why traditionally they are neither buried nor burned. They are laid on the **Towers of Silence**, in Persian **dakhma**, where vultures eat them. Today, though, not all families still follow this custom.

gewusst: The number of Parsis in India has been falling for decades, so there are programmes to keep the community going.
Freddie Mercury grew up partly in India and attended a boarding school there.

teile.einleitung: In Norse mythology, Ragnarök is the end of the world of the gods. After a long winter there is a great battle, and afterwards a new world arises.
wichtigste: Ragnarök literally means “fate of the gods”.
The translation “twilight of the gods” comes from the variant form “ragnarøkkr”.
Before Ragnarök comes the Fimbulwinter, three winters with no summer.
The wolf Fenrir swallows the father of the gods, Odin.
The fire giant Surtr sets the world on fire.
Afterwards the renewed earth rises from the sea.

abschnitte.text: The Old Norse word **Ragnarök** literally means **“fate of the gods”**. You also often hear the translation **“twilight of the gods”**. It comes from a variant form of the word, **ragnarøkkr**. The most important source is the poem **Völuspá**, “the prophecy of the seeress”, from the collection of the Edda.

Before the end of the world comes the **Fimbulwinter**. It consists of three winters in a row, with no summer in between. People quarrel with one another, and order falls apart. The long winter is seen as a sign that the end is near.

At the end of the world, dangerous beings break free. The chained wolf **Fenrir** tears himself loose and swallows the father of the gods, **Odin**. Odin’s son **Vidar** then avenges him. The god **Thor** fights the huge **Midgard Serpent**. Many gods and their enemies fall in this battle.

In the end the fire giant **Surtr** sets the world on fire. He comes from **Muspelheim**, the world of fire. Then the earth sinks into the sea. According to the Völuspá, it later rises again, **renewed** and green. Some gods survive, and two humans also begin a new life.

gewusst: The composer Richard Wagner called one of his best-known operas “Götterdämmerung” (“Twilight of the Gods”).
The story of Ragnarök does not end only with destruction, but with a new beginning.

teile.einleitung: Orishas are deities in the religion of the Yoruba in West Africa. Each Orisha is responsible for particular areas of life and nature. Through enslaved people, belief in the Orishas also reached America.
wichtigste: Orishas are deities of the Yoruba.
Most Yoruba live in south-west Nigeria, with smaller groups in Benin and Togo.
The highest god is called Olodumare, also known as Olorun.
Shango is the Orisha of thunder and lightning, Ogun the Orisha of iron.
The sacred grove of Oshun near Osogbo is a UNESCO World Heritage site.
In Brazil Candomblé arose, in Cuba Santería.

abschnitte.text: The **Yoruba** are a large people in West Africa. Most live in the south-west of **Nigeria**, with smaller groups in **Benin** and **Togo**. Their religion knows a highest creator god, **Olodumare**, also called **Olorun**. He is regarded as far away. That is why people usually turn to the **Orishas**. They are responsible for particular areas of life and nature.

**Shango** rules over **thunder and lightning**. He is also regarded as an early king of the city of **Oyo**. His symbol is a **double axe**. **Ogun** is the Orisha of **iron** and of smiths. He is responsible for tools and war. Today he is also revered by people who work with machines and vehicles, such as drivers and mechanics.

**Oshun** is the goddess of a river. Her sacred **grove** lies near the city of **Osogbo** in Nigeria. It has been a UNESCO World Heritage site since **2005**. A great festival takes place there every year. **Yemanjá** is regarded as the mother of the **sea**. She is especially revered in **Brazil**. For her festivals, people bring flowers and small gifts to the water.

Many Yoruba were carried off to America as **slaves**. They brought their belief in the Orishas with them. In **Brazil**, above all in **Bahia**, **Candomblé** arose from it. In **Cuba** people linked their Orishas with **Catholic saints**. This is how **Santería** arose. In this way they were able to keep their faith alive even when it was banned or despised.

gewusst: On New Year’s Eve in Rio de Janeiro, many people bring flowers for Yemanjá to the sea.
In Yoruba tradition the city of Ile-Ife is regarded as the place where the world was created.

teile.einleitung: Mahavira was an Indian teacher who lived in the 6th or 5th century BC. He is regarded as the most important teacher of Jainism and gave this religion its present form.
wichtigste: Mahavira was actually called Vardhamana and was a prince.
His name means “great hero”.
At about 30 he left his home and lived for twelve years as a strict wandering ascetic.
For the Jains he is the 24th and last Tirthankara of our age.
He lived at about the same time as Buddha in north-eastern India.
The name Jainism comes from “Jina”, which means “victor”.

abschnitte.text: Mahavira was born as a prince with the name **Vardhamana**. At about 30 he gave up his comfortable life. He wandered about as an **ascetic**, that is, a person who gives up almost everything. For twelve years he lived very strictly, fasted often and meditated. After that, according to Jain belief, he attained perfect knowledge.

The name **Mahavira** means “great hero”. What is meant is not a hero in battle, but one who has overcome his own desires. Such a person is called a **Jina**, “victor” or “conqueror”. The name **Jainism** comes from this word. The followers are called Jainas or Jains.

The Jains worship 24 great teachers, the **Tirthankaras**. The word means “ford-makers”: they show the way across the river of rebirths, as a ford leads through a river. Mahavira is the **24th** and last Tirthankara of our age. So he is regarded not as the founder, but as the one who renewed an ancient teaching.

At the centre of Mahavira’s teaching stands **ahimsa**, not harming any living being. Jains eat no meat, and some monks sweep the path in front of them so as not to tread on small animals. Like Buddha, who lived at the same time, Mahavira turned against **animal sacrifice**. An important place of pilgrimage for the Jains is **Shravanabelagola** in Karnataka, with a statue of Bahubali about 17 metres high, which was carved from a single block of granite around 981.

gewusst: The Bahubali statue at Shravanabelagola is among the largest statues in the world made of a single stone.
Mahavira and Buddha lived in the same region of India and were contemporaries.

teile.einleitung: The Middle Way is a basic idea of Buddhism. Buddha taught that neither a life of luxury nor harsh self-torment leads to enlightenment, but a path between these extremes.
wichtigste: The Middle Way lies between luxury and strict asceticism.
Siddhartha Gautama grew up as a prince in a palace.
Later he lived as a strict ascetic and fasted almost to death.
When he gave up asceticism, he is said to have accepted a bowl of rice porridge.
Under a sacred fig tree in Bodh Gaya he reached enlightenment.
Buddha means “the awakened one”.
The Madhyamaka school bears the name “school of the Middle Way”.

abschnitte.titel: From the palace to the wilderness
abschnitte.text: **Siddhartha Gautama** was the son of a ruler from the **Shakya** clan. He grew up in the luxury of a palace and had everything he wanted. But when he saw old age, sickness and death, he left his home. He wanted to find a way to overcome suffering.

Siddhartha lived for years as a strict **ascetic**. He ate almost nothing and became so weak that he nearly died. He realised that this **self-torment** was not getting him anywhere. Tradition tells that a young woman called **Sujata** brought him a bowl of **rice with milk**. Siddhartha accepted it and, strengthened, carried on meditating.

In **Bodh Gaya** in India, Siddhartha sat down under a **sacred fig**, in Latin Ficus religiosa. There, according to tradition, he reached **enlightenment**. That is why the tree is called the **Bodhi tree**, the “tree of awakening”. Since then Siddhartha has borne the honorary title **Buddha**, which means “the awakened one”.

A well-known story explains the **Middle Way** with the strings of a lute. If a string is stretched **too tight**, it snaps. If it is **too loose**, it does not sound. Only when it is tuned just right does it give a beautiful note. In the same way, a person should be neither too strict nor too careless with themselves.

abschnitte.titel: The school of the Middle Way
abschnitte.text: Later the idea of the middle also became important in philosophy. The **Madhyamaka** school in Mahayana Buddhism goes back to the Indian scholar **Nagarjuna**. Its name means “teaching of the middle”. It looks for a path between the view that everything exists firmly and the view that nothing exists at all.

gewusst: In Bodh Gaya today there stands a tree that is regarded as a descendant of the original Bodhi tree.
According to Buddha’s teaching, the Middle Way leads to the Noble Eightfold Path, a path with eight steps.

teile.einleitung: Moses Mendelssohn was a Jewish philosopher in the 18th century. He is regarded as one of the most important thinkers of the Enlightenment in Germany. He argued that people should be free to believe as they choose.
wichtigste: Moses Mendelssohn was born in Dessau in 1729 and died in Berlin in 1786.
His father was a Torah scribe, that is, a man who copied holy writings by hand.
At the age of 14 he followed his teacher to Berlin.
He was a close friend of the poet Gotthold Ephraim Lessing.
Lessing’s character Nathan in “Nathan the Wise” has features of Mendelssohn.
He translated the five books of Moses into German.
The composer Felix Mendelssohn Bartholdy was his grandson.

abschnitte.text: Moses Mendelssohn was born in **Dessau** in 1729. His father was a **Torah scribe**. Moses learned Hebrew and the Jewish writings early on. At the age of 14 he walked to **Berlin**, because his teacher moved there. In Berlin life was hard for Jews at that time, as they had fewer rights than other residents. Moses taught himself German, Latin and other languages.

In Berlin Mendelssohn got to know the poet **Gotthold Ephraim Lessing**. The two became close friends and discussed philosophy and religion a great deal. Lessing later wrote the play **“Nathan the Wise”**. The main character Nathan is a wise and tolerant Jew. Many people see in Nathan a portrait of Moses Mendelssohn. The play argues that people of different religions should respect one another.

Mendelssohn translated the **five books of Moses**, the Torah, into German. But he had the translation printed in **Hebrew letters**. That way many Jews who could read Hebrew could learn standard German. The translation appeared from 1780 together with a Hebrew commentary. In this way Mendelssohn built a bridge between Jewish tradition and German culture.

In 1783 his work **“Jerusalem, or On Religious Power and Judaism”** appeared. In it Mendelssohn demanded that state and religion should be separate. The state should not force anyone to believe anything in particular. Every person has a right to **freedom of conscience**. These ideas are an important part of the **Enlightenment**, a time when people put their trust in reason and freedom.

Moses Mendelssohn’s son Abraham was a banker. His son was the composer **Felix Mendelssohn Bartholdy**, who is world-famous to this day. Felix’s sister **Fanny Hensel** was also a gifted composer. Abraham had his children baptised as Christians. In this way the family became well known over several generations in art, music and business.

gewusst: Mendelssohn was also called “the German Socrates”, after the famous Greek philosopher.
In 1763 he won a prize from the Berlin Academy of Sciences, ahead of the later famous philosopher Immanuel Kant.

teile.einleitung: A Shinto shrine is a holy place of the Japanese religion Shinto. There people revere the kami, the deities and spirits of Shinto. In Japan there are very many shrines, from tiny ones at the roadside to large complexes.
wichtigste: Shinto is the ancient religion of Japan.
Shinto means “way of the gods”.
The beings revered are called kami.
Before praying you cleanse your hands and mouth with water.
When praying you bow twice, clap twice and bow once more.
Foxes are regarded as messengers of the deity Inari.

abschnitte.text: At the entrance to a shrine there is usually a **torii**, a gate made of two posts and two crossbeams. It shows that a sacred area begins here. Many torii are painted bright red. The word **Shinto** consists of two written characters and means “way of the gods”. The beings revered are called **kami**. According to the belief, they live, for example, in mountains, trees or rivers.

Before praying you go to a **water basin**. With a ladle you first rinse your hands and then your mouth. In this way you cleanse yourself before prayer. **Purity** is very important in Shinto. Only afterwards do you go to the prayer hall.

In front of the hall people often throw a coin into an offering box. Then you bow **twice**, clap your hands **twice** and bow once more. With the clapping you greet the kami. Some shrines also have a bell, which you ring beforehand. The prayer is mostly spoken silently.

**Omikuji** are small slips of paper that predict luck or bad luck. If you draw a bad slip, you often tie it to a string or a branch in the shrine. That way the bad luck is meant to stay there. On small wooden plaques called **ema** you write wishes, for example for a good exam result. The plaques are hung up in the shrine.

**Inari** is the deity of rice and the harvest. Foxes are regarded as her messengers. That is why there are many **fox statues** at Inari shrines. The best known is the Fushimi Inari shrine in Kyōto. There thousands of red torii in long corridors lead up a mountain.

gewusst: At the Fushimi Inari shrine in Kyōto, thousands of red gates stand one behind the other.
Anyone who draws a bad fortune slip leaves it behind in the shrine so that the bad luck stays there.
