teile.einleitung: Lourdes is a small town in the south of France and one of the best-known Catholic places of pilgrimage in the world. Every year millions of people make their way there. Many sick people hope for comfort and healing at the spring in the grotto.
wichtigste: Lourdes lies in the south of France at the edge of the Pyrenees.
In 1858 the girl Bernadette Soubirous, by her own account, saw Mary there.
The apparitions took place in the grotto of Massabielle.
Many sick people make a pilgrimage to the spring.
Bernadette was canonised in 1933.

abschnitte.text: **Lourdes** lies in the south of **France** at the edge of the **Pyrenees**, a mountain range on the border with Spain. The river Gave de Pau flows through the town. In the past Lourdes was a small, unknown place. Today it is one of the largest **places of pilgrimage** in the world. There are many churches, hotels and pilgrim hostels there.

In **1858** the girl **Bernadette Soubirous** reported that a woman had appeared to her in a rock grotto. The grotto is called **Massabielle**. According to Bernadette’s accounts she saw the woman 18 times in all. Believers are convinced that it was **Mary**, the mother of Jesus. The Catholic Church later recognised the **apparitions**. Bernadette was canonised in **1933**.

At the grotto a **spring** rises. Many **sick people** come to drink the water or bathe in it. They hope for comfort and **healing**. After careful examination the Church has recognised a small number of healings as unexplained. For many pilgrims, though, it is above all the prayer together that matters. From Switzerland too, organised **pilgrimages** travel to Lourdes every year.

gewusst: In the evening in Lourdes, thousands of pilgrims with burning candles walk in a procession of lights through the holy precinct.
Many pilgrims take water from the spring home with them in small bottles.

teile.einleitung: The Pantheon in Rome is one of the best-preserved buildings of antiquity. With its huge dome and the round opening at the top, it has impressed visitors for almost 1900 years.
wichtigste: “Pantheon” means “all gods”.
The present building was put up roughly between 118 and 125 AD under Emperor Hadrian.
Above the entrance stands the name of Marcus Agrippa.
The dome has a diameter of about 43 metres and is made of Roman concrete.
The round opening at the top is called the oculus.
Since 609 AD the Pantheon has been a Christian church.
The painter Raphael is buried here.

abschnitte.titel: A temple for all the gods
abschnitte.text: The name comes from Greek: **pan** means all and **theos** means god. The temple was probably dedicated to many gods. A first building was put up by **Marcus Agrippa**, a friend of Emperor Augustus. The present building was put up under Emperor **Hadrian**. When rebuilding, he had the old inscription with Agrippa’s name put in place.

The dome measures about **43 metres** across. To this day it is the largest dome made of **unreinforced concrete**, that is, without steel inside. The Romans mixed lime, volcanic ash and stones into concrete. At the top they used lighter stones so that the dome weighs less. The interior is exactly as high as it is wide, so a sphere would fit inside exactly.

At the very top of the dome there is a round opening, the **oculus**. It is about 9 metres across. Apart from the entrance, it is the only source of light in the interior. Depending on the time of day, a bright circle of light moves over the walls and floor. When it rains, the water falls in and drains away through small holes in the floor.

In the year **609** Pope **Boniface IV** consecrated the building as the church of Santa Maria ad Martyres. Because it was now a church, it was not pulled down and so stayed well preserved. Services are still held there today.

The painter **Raphael** died in Rome in 1520. At his own wish he was buried in the Pantheon. Later Italian kings were also buried there, such as Victor Emmanuel II. The Pantheon served many master builders as a model for their own domes.

gewusst: The dome of the Pantheon has not collapsed in almost 1900 years, although it has no steel reinforcement.
The inscription above the entrance says in Latin that Marcus Agrippa built it, although the present building dates from Hadrian.

teile.einleitung: The Sikh gurus are the ten teachers who founded and shaped Sikhism. They lived from the 15th to the 18th century in the Punjab. After the tenth guru, the holy scripture itself is regarded as the eternal guru.
wichtigste: Sikhism arose around 1500 in the Punjab.
Guru Nanak was the founder and first guru.
Guru Ram Das founded the city of Amritsar.
Guru Arjan had the Golden Temple built.
Guru Tegh Bahadur was executed in Delhi in 1675.
Today the scripture Guru Granth Sahib is regarded as the guru.

abschnitte.text: The **Punjab** is a region that today belongs to India and Pakistan. The name means “land of five rivers”. **Guru Nanak** lived there from 1469 to 1539. He taught that there is only one God and that all people are of equal worth. He is the first of the ten gurus. **Guru** means teacher.

**Guru Ram Das**, the fourth guru, founded the city of **Amritsar** in the 16th century. He had a holy pool laid out there. His successor **Guru Arjan** had the **Harmandir Sahib**, the Golden Temple, built in the middle of it. He also compiled the first collection of holy texts. In 1606 he was executed on the orders of the Mughal emperor and is regarded as the first martyr of the Sikhs.

**Guru Hargobind**, the sixth guru, carried two swords. They are called **Miri** and **Piri** and stand for worldly and spiritual power. In this way he showed that the Sikhs should also defend themselves. **Guru Har Krishan** became the eighth guru in 1661 while still a small child. He died of smallpox at about eight years old.

abschnitte.titel: Standing up for freedom of belief
abschnitte.text: **Guru Tegh Bahadur**, the ninth guru, stood up for persecuted Hindus. He was executed in **Delhi** in 1675 on the orders of the Mughal emperor **Aurangzeb**. Sikhs remember him as a fighter for freedom of belief. At the place in Delhi there is a well-known Sikh temple today.

**Guru Gobind Singh** was the tenth guru. In 1699 he founded the **Khalsa**, the community of baptised Sikhs. Before his death in 1708 he decreed that after him no human being should be guru any more. Instead the holy scripture **Guru Granth Sahib** is regarded as the eternal guru. It is kept with ceremony in every Sikh temple.

gewusst: In the Golden Temple in Amritsar, a great many visitors receive a free meal every day, whatever religion they belong to.
The eighth guru was still a small child when he became guru.

teile.einleitung: In November, in many places in Switzerland, children walk through the dark streets with glowing lanterns. The lanterns are carved from turnips and are called Räbeliechtli. The custom is one of the loveliest of the autumn season.
wichtigste: A **Räbeliechtli** is a lantern made from a hollowed-out turnip.
**Räben** are white turnips.
Patterns are carved into the turnip and a candle is put inside.
At the **Räbeliechtli procession**, children walk through the streets in November.
People sing songs such as “Räbeliechtli, wo gaasch hii?” (“Little turnip light, where are you going?”).

abschnitte.text: A **Räbe** is a white turnip that is harvested in autumn. In the past it was an important vegetable and food for animals. For the Räbeliechtli, the turnip is hollowed out with a spoon or a special tool. Then patterns are carved into the skin, for example stars, moons or faces. Finally a candle is put inside and the turnip is hung on a string from a stick.

In November, when it gets dark early, the **Räbeliechtli procession** takes place in many municipalities. The children walk in a long line through the streets, often with their school or nursery. The street lamps are sometimes switched off for this, so that the lanterns shine better. The children sing Räbeliechtli songs as they go. The custom is widespread above all in German-speaking Switzerland.

Where exactly the custom comes from is not entirely certain. It has to do with the end of the harvest and the dark season. In some areas it is linked with **St Martin’s Day** on 11 November, when lantern processions take place in many countries. Especially well known is the **Räbechilbi** in **Richterswil** on Lake Zurich, at which whole houses and floats are decorated with carved turnips.

gewusst: For the Räbechilbi in Richterswil, several tonnes of turnips are carved every year.
In many nurseries and schools, turnip carving is a fixed part of autumn.

teile.einleitung: Shalom is one of the best-known Hebrew words. It means peace and is used as a greeting. Jews all over the world know it.
wichtigste: **Shalom** means peace.
It comes from **Hebrew**.
In Israel people say shalom when greeting and when saying goodbye.
Shalom also means **well-being** and wholeness.
The Arabic word **salam** is related to shalom.
“Shalom aleichem” means “peace be upon you”.

abschnitte.text: Shalom means **peace**. But it does not mean only that there is no quarrel or war. The word also means that you are well, that you are healthy and that everything is whole and sound. In the Hebrew Bible shalom occurs very often. Anyone who wishes someone shalom is therefore wishing them everything good.

In **Israel** people greet each other with shalom both on arriving and on leaving. So it is like “hello” and “goodbye” at once. A longer, friendly greeting is “**Shalom aleichem**”, which means “peace be upon you”. On the Sabbath people wish each other “Shabbat shalom”, a peaceful Sabbath.

**Hebrew** and **Arabic** are related languages. That is why there are many similar words. The Arabic **salam** likewise means peace, and the greeting “Salam aleikum” is very like “Shalom aleichem”. The name of the city of **Jerusalem** is also often linked with the word shalom.

“**Hevenu shalom aleichem**” is a well-known Hebrew song. The title means “We bring peace to you”. It is sung all over the world, including in Swiss schools and churches. Often people sing it in a circle and clap along.

gewusst: Shalom is also a first name in Israel, and there are many names that contain the word, such as Solomon.
With the one word shalom you can greet, say goodbye and wish peace.

teile.einleitung: Secular humanism is an outlook on life without belief in God or supernatural powers. It bases ethics and morality on reason, science and compassion. Around the world there are organisations that stand for this outlook.
wichtigste: Secular humanists reject supernatural explanations.
Ethics should be based on reason, science and compassion.
The first “Humanist Manifesto” appeared in the USA in 1933.
Paul Kurtz published “A Secular Humanist Declaration” in 1980.
The worldwide umbrella organisation was founded in Amsterdam in 1952.
World Humanist Day is on 21 June.

abschnitte.text: **Secular** means worldly, that is, not religious. **Secular humanists** do not believe in God or supernatural forces. They base ethics and morality on **reason**, **science** and **compassion**. For them, people themselves are responsible for a good life and a just society. Human rights, democracy and free thought are important to them.

The first “**Humanist Manifesto**” appeared in the USA in **1933**. Among others it was signed by the philosopher **John Dewey**. Later versions appeared in 1973 and 2003. In 1980 the American philosopher **Paul Kurtz** published “A Secular Humanist Declaration”. Kurtz also founded the Council for Secular Humanism and is regarded as an important organiser of the movement.

In 1952 the International Humanist and Ethical Union was founded in **Amsterdam**. Its first president was the biologist **Julian Huxley**. Since 2019 it has been called **Humanists International**. In 2002 it adopted the **Amsterdam Declaration** and renewed it in 2022. This describes humanism as an ethical, rational and democratic outlook on life.

Many humanist organisations use the **Happy Human** symbol. It shows a stylised figure with raised arms. **Dennis Barrington** designed it in 1965 for the British Humanist Association. **World Humanist Day** falls on **21 June**, the solstice in the Northern Hemisphere. On this day humanists draw attention to their values.

In Switzerland too there are organisations of people with no denomination, such as the **Freethinkers**. They campaign, for example, for the separation of state and church. Some also offer secular ceremonies, for example for weddings or funerals. Critics from religious communities argue, by contrast, that faith gives many people support and direction.

gewusst: The Happy Human symbol came about in 1965 from a competition in Great Britain.
World Humanist Day falls on the longest day of the year in the Northern Hemisphere.

teile.einleitung: “I am the light of the world” is a famous saying of Jesus from the Bible. For Christians, light is therefore an important sign of Jesus. You find it in churches, at festivals and in many customs.
wichtigste: In the Gospel of John, Jesus says: “I am the light of the world.”
For Christians, light is a sign of Jesus.
In the Sermon on the Mount, Jesus says to the people: “You are the light of the world.”
Candles in church recall this light.
At Easter a large Easter candle is lit.

abschnitte.text: In the **Gospel of John**, **Jesus** says: “I am the light of the world. Whoever follows me will not walk in darkness.” By this he means that he shows people the way, as a light does in the dark. In the **Sermon on the Mount** Jesus also says to his listeners: “You are the light of the world.” So Christians themselves should do good and shine for others.

In churches **candles** often burn. Many people light a candle when they pray or think of someone. At **Easter** a large **Easter candle** is lit. It stands for Jesus, who according to Christian belief rose from the dead. At **Christmas**, too, the many lights recall that for Christians Jesus is the light of the world.

Light is a strong sign in other religions too. The Bible itself begins with the words “Let there be light”. Jews celebrate a festival of lights at **Hanukkah**, Hindus at **Diwali**. In Advent, the **Peace Light** from Bethlehem is handed out in Switzerland. Light stands for hope, warmth and what is good.

gewusst: The Peace Light is lit every year in the Grotto of the Nativity in Bethlehem and then taken to many countries.
The saying “I am the light of the world” is in the 8th chapter of the Gospel of John.

teile.einleitung: A mezuzah is a small case on the doorpost of Jewish homes and houses. Inside it is a scroll with sentences from the Torah, meant to remind people of God’s commandments.
wichtigste: The Hebrew word mezuzah means “doorpost”.
The case holds a small, handwritten scroll.
On it is written, among other things, the prayer “Hear, O Israel”, in Hebrew “Shema Yisrael”.
The mezuzah hangs on the right-hand doorpost as you go in.
In many families it hangs at a slant, with its top end pointing into the room.
On the outside there is often the Hebrew letter Shin.
Many people touch the mezuzah as they go through and then kiss their fingers.

abschnitte.text: The word **mezuzah** means “doorpost” in Hebrew. So the small case is named after the place where it hangs. You find it on the front door and often on the room doors of Jewish homes. The case can be made of wood, metal, glass or stone and is often beautifully decorated. The plural is **mezuzot**.

Inside the case lies a small **scroll** of parchment. A trained scribe writes it by hand. On it are two passages from the **Torah**, the five books of Moses. The first begins with the words **“Hear, O Israel”**, in Hebrew “Shema Yisrael”. It is one of the most important prayers in Judaism. This text also contains the commandment to write God’s words on the doorposts of the house.

The mezuzah is fixed to the **right-hand doorpost** as you enter the room. It hangs in the upper third of the post. In many families, especially among Ashkenazi Jews, it hangs **at a slant**. The top end points into the room. This position came about as a compromise between scholars who wanted it vertical or horizontal.

On the outside there is often the Hebrew letter **Shin**. It stands for a name of God. Many people **touch** the mezuzah with their fingers as they go through and then kiss their fingers. This shows respect for God’s word. Each time you go out and come in, the mezuzah reminds you of faith.

gewusst: The scroll of a mezuzah is checked regularly by an expert, because even one damaged letter can make it invalid.
In Israel mezuzot also hang on many doors of public buildings.

teile.einleitung: Samsara is a concept from Hinduism and other religions of India. It denotes the cycle of birth, death and rebirth. Many believers hope one day to be freed from this cycle.
wichtigste: **Samsara** is the cycle of birth, death and rebirth.
**Karma** determines above all the next birth.
Karma literally means “deed” or “action”.
According to the belief, you can also be reborn as an animal.
Liberation from the cycle is called **moksha**.
Buddhism, Jainism and Sikhism also know rebirth.

abschnitte.text: According to Hindu belief, the soul does not die with the body. After death it is reborn in a new body. This endless cycle is called **samsara**. The word comes from **Sanskrit**, an ancient language of India. Depending on your own deeds, you can be reborn as a human, as an animal or in other forms of existence.

The Sanskrit word **karma** means “deed” or “action”. What is meant is that every action has consequences for the future. Good and bad deeds leave effects that influence the next life. According to this belief, anyone who does good can hope for a better life.

A well-known image comes from the **Bhagavad Gita**, a sacred text of Hinduism. Just as a person takes off old clothes and puts on new ones, so the soul leaves the old body and takes on a new one. The image is meant to show that the soul itself stays unchanged. Only its outer covering changes.

The highest goal of many Hindus is **moksha**, which means “liberation”. Anyone who reaches moksha is no longer reborn. Ways to it are, for example, good conduct, knowledge, meditation and devotion to God. **Buddhism**, **Jainism** and **Sikhism** also teach a cycle of rebirths. In Buddhism the liberation is called **nirvana**.

gewusst: The word samsara originally means something like “wandering” or “passing through”.
Because animals too are said to have a soul, many Hindus live as vegetarians.

teile.einleitung: Nagarjuna was a Buddhist philosopher from India. He probably lived in the 2nd century AD. He is regarded as one of the most important thinkers of Mahayana Buddhism and founded the school of the Middle Way.
wichtigste: Nagarjuna probably lived roughly between 150 and 250 AD, most likely in southern India.
The Madhyamaka school, the “school of the Middle”, goes back to him.
His main work is called the Mulamadhyamakakarika, the “Fundamental Verses on the Middle Way”.
He taught that all things are “empty” of intrinsic nature.
Emptiness does not mean that nothing exists.
He distinguished between a conventional and an ultimate truth.
Later scholars such as Chandrakirti developed his teaching further.

abschnitte.text: Little is known for certain about Nagarjuna’s life. Usually it is assumed that he lived roughly between **150 and 250 AD**, probably in **southern India**. Many legends surround him. One tells that he received the **Prajnaparamita sutras** from the **Nagas**. These are serpent beings from Indian mythology. They are said to have guarded the texts in their realm until the time was ripe.

Nagarjuna founded the **Madhyamaka** school. The name means “school of the Middle”. It looks for a path between two extremes: the view that things exist firmly and for ever, and the view that nothing exists at all. His main work is called the **Mulamadhyamakakarika**, the “Fundamental Verses on the Middle Way”. In 27 chapters he examines ideas such as motion, time and cause.

A central concept is **emptiness**, in Sanskrit **shunyata**. According to Nagarjuna, all things are empty of **intrinsic nature** (svabhava). That means: nothing exists entirely on its own. Everything depends on something else. This dependence is called **dependent origination**. In the 24th chapter of the Fundamental Verses he equates emptiness with dependent origination. So emptiness does not mean that nothing is there.

Nagarjuna distinguishes **two truths**. On the **conventional** level we speak quite normally of things and persons. On the **ultimate** level everything shows itself to be empty. He also uses the **tetralemma**, in Sanskrit catuskoti. It examines four possibilities: something is, is not, is both, or is neither. Nagarjuna shows that none of these four statements fully captures reality.

Nagarjuna’s teaching was developed further by many scholars. In the 7th century **Chandrakirti** defended the so-called **Prasangika** interpretation against the scholar Bhavaviveka. In it, opposing views are only led into their contradictions, without putting forward a firm claim of one’s own. Chandrakirti’s interpretation became authoritative in **Tibetan Buddhism**. Nagarjuna is also greatly revered in China and Japan.

gewusst: In several Buddhist schools of East Asia, Nagarjuna is regarded as an important patriarch, that is, one of the great teachers of the tradition.
In Tibet, Nagarjuna is often revered as the “second Buddha”.

teile.einleitung: Santería is a religion that arose in Cuba. It combines forms of belief of the Yoruba of West Africa with Catholic Christianity. At its centre are deities called orishas.
wichtigste: **Santería** arose in Cuba from the religion of the **Yoruba** and Catholicism.
Many believers prefer to call it **Regla de Ocha** or **Lucumí**.
The deities are called **orishas** and are linked with Catholic saints.
The **babalawo** interprets the oracle of Ifá.
Newly initiated people wear white clothing for a year.
In 1993 the US Supreme Court ruled in favour of Santería.

abschnitte.text: Many people of the **Yoruba** people in West Africa were taken to Cuba as slaves. There they were not allowed to live their religion openly and had to become Catholic. They linked their deities, the **orishas**, with Catholic **saints**. Out of this Santería arose. The name means roughly “worship of saints” and was originally a disparaging name given by outsiders. That is why many believers prefer to say **Regla de Ocha** or **Lucumí**. Lucumí is also the name of the ritual Yoruba language in Cuba.

The thunder god **Changó** is linked with Saint **Barbara**, who is associated with lightning and fire and is shown in red. Her feast day on 4 December is also a festival for Changó. **Ochún**, the orisha of rivers and fresh water, is identified with the **Virgen de la Caridad del Cobre**, the patron saint of Cuba. **Babalú-Ayé**, the lord of diseases, corresponds to Saint **Lazarus**. On 17 December many believers make a pilgrimage to the shrine of El Rincón near Havana.

The **babalawo**, literally “father of secrets”, consults the **Ifá oracle** with a chain or with palm nuts. In the Cuban tradition this office is open only to men. A person who is initiated into the religion is afterwards called an **iyawó**. After the initiation, the “asiento”, the person counts as newborn. They dress entirely in white for a year and keep further rules of conduct.

Some rituals of Santería include **animal sacrifice**. The city of **Hialeah** in Florida passed ordinances that specifically banned these sacrifices. In 1993 the Supreme Court of the USA decided the case “Church of the Lukumi Babalu Aye v. City of Hialeah”. The justices unanimously declared the ordinances unconstitutional, because they violated **freedom of religion**.

gewusst: Similar religions with African roots also exist in Brazil, for example Candomblé.
In Santería the colour white stands for purity and a new beginning.

teile.einleitung: “Ren” is an important concept from the teaching of the Chinese thinker Confucius. It is usually translated as “humaneness”. Ren describes how a good person treats others.
wichtigste: **Ren** roughly means humaneness or kindness.
For Confucius, Ren was the highest virtue.
The written character is made up of the parts for “person” and “two”.
The **Golden Rule** is part of the core of Ren.
In Confucius, the exemplary person is called the **junzi**.

abschnitte.text: **Confucius** lived in China about 2,500 years ago. His teaching is called **Confucianism**. For him, Ren is the highest virtue, that is, the most important good quality. It means kindness and humanity towards others. The Chinese character is made up of the parts for “person” and “two”: Ren shows itself where people live together.

In the **Analects of Confucius** there is the rule: “Do not do to others what you would not want done to yourself.” Confucius words it as a prohibition. It is regarded as the core of Ren, because you infer how others feel from your own feelings. Similar rules are found in many other religions and teachings.

abschnitte.titel: The noble person and his pupils
abschnitte.text: The exemplary person who puts Ren into practice is called the **junzi** by Confucius. Literally this means “prince’s son”, but what is meant is a person who is noble through his character. His opposite is the **xiaoren**, the small or mean person. Of his favourite pupil **Yan Hui**, Confucius said that his heart did not depart from Ren for three months. The other pupils kept it up only for a short time.

gewusst: Yan Hui was regarded as the most gifted pupil of Confucius, but he died young, which saddened Confucius greatly.

teile.einleitung: A rangoli is a colourful picture on the ground. In India many families decorate the entrance to their house with one, especially at festivals such as Diwali.
wichtigste: A rangoli is a coloured pattern on the ground.
It is often laid in front of the front door, usually early in the morning.
It is made of coloured powder, sand, rice flour or flower petals.
The powder is mostly sprinkled with the fingers.
Many rangolis are symmetrical.
At Diwali especially many rangolis are made.

abschnitte.text: A **rangoli** is a coloured pattern on the ground. It is laid or sprinkled by hand. It often decorates the ground **in front of the entrance** of a house or a temple. It is usually made early in the morning. A rangoli is meant to welcome guests and bring **good luck** to the house.

**Coloured powder** or coloured sand is sprinkled into a pattern. Very often white **rice flour** from the kitchen is used. Small animals such as ants may eat some of it, which is regarded as a good deed. Some rangolis are also laid from colourful **flower petals**. Then they smell lovely too.

The powder is mostly sprinkled onto the ground between the **fingers**. This produces fine lines. Many patterns are **symmetrical**, that is, the same on all sides. You often see flowers, circles, stars or lamps. In southern India, similar patterns made of dots and lines are called **kolam**.

Especially many rangolis are made at the festival of lights, **Diwali**. Then many families decorate their entrance with a large, colourful pattern. They often add small oil lamps. Sometimes there are even competitions for the most beautiful rangoli.

gewusst: A rangoli does not last long: wind, rain and footsteps smudge it, so it is often made anew.
The word rangoli comes from Sanskrit and has to do with “colour”.

teile.einleitung: Kosher is the name for food that is permitted under the Jewish dietary laws. The word means “fit” or “suitable”. The rules come from the Torah and are followed closely by many devout Jews.
wichtigste: Kosher means “fit” or “suitable”.
The dietary laws are called kashrut and come from the Torah.
Meat and milk are strictly kept separate.
Only fish with fins and scales are permitted.
Pork is not kosher.
Many families have separate crockery for meat and milk.

abschnitte.text: The Jewish dietary laws are called **kashrut**. They are found in the **Torah**, the most important part of the Hebrew Bible, and were interpreted exactly by rabbis. Food that is permitted is called **kosher**. Food that is not permitted is called **treif**. For many devout Jews these rules are part of everyday life.

Of land animals, only those that **chew the cud** and have **split hooves** are permitted, such as cattle, sheep and goats. The **pig** is not one of them. Of the creatures from the water, only those that have **fins and scales** are kosher. Mussels, crabs and squid are therefore not permitted. Slaughter also follows exact rules, called **shechita**.

A well-known rule is: **meat and milk** are not eaten together. A cheese sandwich with ham would therefore be doubly forbidden. Many families have **separate crockery**, pots and cutlery for this. After a meat meal, people wait several hours before eating dairy products. Foods such as vegetables, fruit or fish count as **neutral** and go with both.

In Switzerland, slaughter without stunning has been forbidden since **1893**. At that time the first federal **popular initiative** was accepted. That is why kosher meat is imported from abroad. In cities such as Zurich, Basel and Geneva there are shops and restaurants with kosher food. A sign on the packaging shows that a rabbi has checked the product.

gewusst: For the festival of Passover, extra rules apply: then no leavened bread is eaten.
Gummy bears too are often not kosher, because gelatine is mostly made from pork.

teile.einleitung: A rabbi is a teacher and leader of a Jewish community. He knows the holy scriptures very well and helps people with questions about faith and everyday life.
wichtigste: A rabbi teaches and advises a Jewish community.
Rabbi means “my teacher” or “my master”.
He often works in the synagogue.
He explains above all the Torah and other Jewish writings.
A woman in this office is called a female rabbi.
Rabbis may marry and have children.

abschnitte.text: The word **rabbi** is Hebrew and means “my teacher” or “my master”. This is how scholars used to be addressed. A **rabbi** has studied the **Torah** and other writings such as the **Talmud** for a long time. He explains them to the people in the community and teaches children and adults.

The **synagogue** is the Jewish place of worship. There the rabbi preaches and teaches. He also accompanies people at important events in life, for example at a boy’s **bar mitzvah**, at weddings and at funerals. A rabbi is not a priest who makes sacrifices, but above all a scholar.

Many people ask the rabbi how they should live by the religious rules. For example, whether a meal is **kosher**. Kosher means that the food is permitted under the Jewish dietary laws. Rabbis know these rules and check, for example, foods and restaurants.

Rabbis may marry and have a family, which is even usual. In many liberal Jewish communities there are also **female rabbis**. The first female rabbi in the world was **Regina Jonas** from Berlin. She was ordained, that is, installed in her office, in 1935. In Orthodox communities, however, only men are rabbis.

gewusst: Training to become a rabbi often takes many years and ends with an ordination, in Hebrew semikha.
In the Gospels, too, Jesus was called “Rabbi” by his disciples.

teile.einleitung: A stupa is a Buddhist structure with a round dome. In many stupas relics are kept, that is, remains of the Buddha or of holy people. Stupas are found all over Asia, and in every country they have their own form.
wichtigste: A stupa mostly has the shape of a dome with a spire.
In many stupas lie relics of holy people.
Believers walk round a stupa clockwise.
Large eyes are painted on the stupa of Boudhanath in Kathmandu.
In East Asia the pagoda developed from the stupa.
The stupas of Sanchi in India are among the oldest buildings of Buddhism.

abschnitte.text: A **stupa** is a structure with a round **dome**. At the top it often has a spire or a small tower. In many stupas lie **relics**, that is, remains of the Buddha or of holy people. That is why stupas are holy places. A stupa recalls the Buddha and his teaching.
Believers walk **clockwise** round the stupa. In doing so they always keep it on their right. Often they pray as they go or turn prayer wheels. This circuit is a form of devotion and of meditation.

The stupas of **Sanchi** in **India** are among the oldest buildings of Buddhism. They are a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The stupa of **Boudhanath** stands in **Kathmandu**, the capital of Nepal, and is one of the largest in the world. Large **eyes** are painted on its tower, looking in all four directions. The **Shwedagon Pagoda** in Yangon in Myanmar is covered with **gold** and shines far over the city.

**Borobudur** on the island of Java in **Indonesia** is the largest Buddhist temple in the world. On its terraces stand many small stupas with Buddha figures inside. In China and Japan the stupa developed into a tall tower with many roofs one above another. It is called a **pagoda**. In Tibet the stupa is called a **chorten**.

gewusst: The eyes on the stupa of Boudhanath look in all four cardinal directions.
According to tradition, the emperor Ashoka had very many stupas built in ancient India.

teile.einleitung: Masks cover the face and transform a person into another being. All over the world they are worn at festivals, dances and customs, including in many Swiss traditions.
wichtigste: Many African masks are carved from wood.
At many festivals the mask wearer represents a spirit or a being.
The Dogon people in Mali are known for their mask dances.
In the Lötschental in Valais, the Tschäggättä wear wild wooden masks.
At the Basel carnival, the masks are called Larven.
In Urnäsch, the Silvesterchläuse go from farm to farm with bells.
The mask carnival in Venice is also famous.

abschnitte.text: According to many old beliefs, anyone who wears a mask becomes another being. In some cultures people believe that the wearer becomes a **spirit** or an ancestor. That is why it often stays secret who is behind the mask. In some **winter customs**, loud, wild figures are supposed to drive away winter and evil spirits. That is why such masks often look frightening.

Many African masks are carved from **wood**. They are often decorated with paint, shells or feathers. The **Dogon** in Mali are especially well known. They dance wearing tall, carved masks. Their dances honour the dead and tell of the creation of the world.

In the **Lötschental** in the canton of Valais there are the **Tschäggättä**. They wear grim, carved wooden masks and the skins of sheep or goats. During the carnival season they go through the villages and frighten people. The masks are made by hand by carvers in the valley.

At the **Basel carnival** the revellers wear large masks called **Larven**. They are mostly made of **papier-mâché** and are often huge, with long noses. With drums and piccolos the cliques march through the city for three days. The Basel carnival is part of UNESCO’s intangible cultural heritage.

In **Urnäsch** in Appenzellerland, the **Silvesterchläuse** go from farm to farm and wish everyone a happy new year. They wear large **bells and cowbells** that ring loudly through the village. They come on New Year’s Eve and on 13 January, the old New Year’s Eve. Outside Switzerland, the carnival in **Venice** is famous, where many people wear elaborate masks and costumes.

gewusst: The Urnäsch Silvesterchläuse celebrate twice, because 13 January was New Year’s Eve in the old Julian calendar.
The German word “Larve” for a mask is the same word that is used for the larva of a butterfly.

teile.einleitung: The Qur’an is the holy book of Islam. For Muslims it contains the word of God, revealed to the Prophet Muhammad. That is why the book is treated with great respect.
wichtigste: The Qur’an is the holy book of Muslims.
It is written in the Arabic language.
It consists of 114 sections called surahs.
According to Islamic belief it was revealed to Muhammad over many years.
Out of respect, a Qur’an is never put on the floor.

abschnitte.text: The word **Qur’an** means “reading” or “recitation”. According to Islamic belief, God brought the words to the Prophet **Muhammad** through the angel **Gabriel**. This happened in the 7th century over about 23 years. The Qur’an is written in **Arabic**. For many Muslims, translations count only as an explanation, not as the actual Qur’an.

The Qur’an consists of **114 surahs**, that is, sections. Each surah is divided into verses. The first surah is called the **Fatiha**, “the Opening”, and is said in every prayer. The surahs are arranged roughly by length, with the long ones coming first. Someone who knows the whole Qur’an by heart is called a **hafiz**.

Because the Qur’an is the word of God for Muslims, they handle the book very carefully. It is **never put on the floor** and nothing is placed on top of it. Often it lies on a stand or a raised place. Many Muslims wash before they touch it. In the fasting month of **Ramadan**, many read the whole Qur’an.

gewusst: Many children learn early on to recite parts of the Qur’an from memory in Arabic.
Verses of the Qur’an are often written in beautiful script, calligraphy, on mosques.

teile.einleitung: Shichi-Go-San is a Japanese festival for children. Families celebrate with it that their children have reached a certain age in good health. For this they visit a Shinto shrine.
wichtigste: Shichi-Go-San means “seven, five, three”.
The festival is traditionally celebrated on 15 November.
Girls are celebrated at three and seven years old and boys at five.
Families visit a Shinto shrine and give thanks for the children’s health.
Many children wear a festive kimono for it.
The children receive long sweets called chitose-ame.

abschnitte.text: In Japanese, **shichi** is seven, **go** is five and **san** is three. What is meant is the age of the children who are celebrated. Traditionally **girls** are celebrated at three and seven years old and **boys** at five. In some regions three-year-old boys are celebrated too. Odd numbers are regarded as lucky in Japan.

The traditional festival day is **15 November**. Today many families also go on the weekends before or after. They visit a **Shinto shrine** and give thanks for the children growing up healthy. They ask the **kami**, the deities of Shinto, for a long and happy life. Often souvenir photos are taken afterwards.

Many children put on a festive **kimono** for the first time. Boys often wear a **hakama** with it, wide pleated trousers. Some families hire the clothes because they are very valuable. Some children also wear Western festive clothes today.

The children receive **chitose-ame**, which means “thousand-year sweets”. They are long sticks of candy coloured red and white. The long shape stands for a long life. The bag is decorated with **cranes** and **tortoises**, which in Japan likewise stand for long life.

abschnitte.titel: Why the festival was so important
abschnitte.text: In the past, many children in Japan died very young, and **child mortality** was high. When a child reached a certain age, people therefore gave special thanks for its survival. The custom is several centuries old. Today it is above all a cheerful family festival.

gewusst: The crane and tortoise on the sweet bag stand for a long life in Japan.
The name of the festival is simply made up of three numbers.

teile.einleitung: Krishna is one of the most popular gods in Hinduism. Hindus believe that he is an appearance of the god Vishnu. Many stories tell of his cheerful childhood, his flute and his wisdom.
wichtigste: Krishna is an appearance of the god Vishnu.
He is often shown with blue skin and a peacock feather in his hair.
Krishna plays the flute.
As a boy he tended the cows among cowherds.
The little Krishna liked to nibble butter.
His birthday is called Janmashtami.
According to the story, he was born in Mathura.

abschnitte.text: Krishna is often painted with **blue** or dark skin. The colour recalls the sky and the sea. In his hair he often wears a colourful **peacock feather**, and in his hand he holds a **flute**. By these you recognise him at once in pictures. With his music he is said to have enchanted everyone.

Hindus believe that the god **Vishnu** came to earth in various forms to protect the world. Such an appearance is called an **avatar**. Krishna is regarded as one of the most important avatars of Vishnu. Many Hindus also worship him as the highest god.

According to the story, Krishna was born in the city of **Mathura** in the north of India. He grew up among **cowherds** and as a boy tended the **cows**. The little Krishna secretly nibbled **butter** from the pots, so he is also called the **butter thief**. In many songs and stories **Radha** is his dearest friend, and the two are often shown together.

In the great epic **Mahabharata**, Krishna as an adult is adviser to the hero **Arjuna**. He drives his chariot. Before a great battle he explains to him how to act rightly. This conversation is called the **Bhagavad Gita** and is one of the most important scriptures of Hinduism.

On **Janmashtami** Hindus celebrate Krishna’s birthday. Many fast during the day and stay awake until **midnight**, because he is said to have been born at that time. People sing songs, decorate temples and act out scenes from his life. In Mathura the festival is celebrated especially grandly. Hindus in Switzerland also celebrate it in their temples.

gewusst: In a game on Janmashtami, young people form a human pyramid to reach a pot of butter or yoghurt hung up high.
The Hare Krishna movement has made the name Krishna known in Europe too.

teile.einleitung: Siddhartha Gautama is the man who was later called the Buddha. He lived about 2,500 years ago in India and founded Buddhism. Buddha means “the awakened one”.
wichtigste: The Buddha was really called Siddhartha Gautama.
He was born in Lumbini, which today lies in Nepal.
He was a prince, son of King Suddhodana and Queen Maya.
He lived about 2,500 years ago; the exact year is uncertain.
He left the palace to find the cause of suffering.
According to tradition he lived to be about 80.

abschnitte.text: **Siddhartha Gautama** was born in **Lumbini**. This place lies today in **Nepal**, near the border with India. His father was King **Suddhodana**, who ruled over the small kingdom of the Shakyas. His mother was Queen **Maya**. According to tradition she died shortly after his birth, so her sister brought him up.

His father wanted Siddhartha to become **king** later. That is why he was to stay in the palace and see nothing sad. He lived in luxury with beautiful gardens and festivals. But according to the legend, he left the palace a few times. On these trips he saw an old person, a sick person, a dead person and a monk. These **four encounters** changed his life.

At about 29, Siddhartha left the palace. For several years he lived very strictly as an ascetic and ate almost nothing. But he realised that this was getting him nowhere. He chose a **middle way** between luxury and hunger. Under a fig tree in **Bodhgaya** he meditated and attained **enlightenment**. From then on he was called the **Buddha**, the awakened one.

The Buddha gave his first sermon in a park near **Sarnath**. He explained where suffering comes from and how it can be overcome. Many people followed him, and a community of monks and nuns formed. Until his death he travelled about and taught. According to tradition he lived to be about **80** years old.

gewusst: Lumbini, the birthplace of the Buddha, is today a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
The tree under which the Buddha meditated is called the Bodhi tree, “tree of awakening”.

teile.einleitung: A mandala is a picture, usually circular, with a clear centre. In Buddhism and Hinduism it represents a holy world and helps with meditation.
wichtigste: The Sanskrit word “mandala” means circle.
In Buddhism mandalas serve above all as an aid to meditation.
In the centre there is usually a Buddha or a deity.
Many Tibetan mandalas show a square with four gates inside a circle.
Tibetan monks scatter mandalas of coloured sand and then destroy them again.
The Swiss psychologist Carl Gustav Jung took an interest in mandalas.

abschnitte.text: **Mandala** is a word from **Sanskrit**, an ancient Indian language, and means “circle”. A mandala is a symmetrical picture arranged around a centre. The **centre** is the most important point. There a Buddha or a deity is usually shown, around whom everything else is ordered.

In many Tibetan mandalas you see inside the circle a **square with four gates**. It represents a palace. The gates face the **four points of the compass**. Whoever looks at the mandala is led by the eyes from the outside inwards to the centre. In this way you are meant to find inner calm. That is why the mandala serves above all as an aid to **meditation**.

Tibetan monks scatter special mandalas of **coloured sand**. With fine tubes they lay grain after grain for days into an artistic picture. When it is finished, it is **destroyed** again. The sand is swept together and often scattered in a river. This is meant to show that nothing in the world lasts for ever.

The Swiss psychologist **Carl Gustav Jung** from Küsnacht near Zurich painted mandalas himself. He saw in them a picture of the **wholeness of the soul**. He also had his patients paint mandalas. Today many children colour in mandalas at school, because it can be calming.

Some temples are built like a mandala. The best-known example is **Borobudur** on the island of Java in Indonesia. It was built around the year 800. Seen from above, the huge complex resembles a mandala made of stone. Pilgrims walk around it step by step up to the top.

gewusst: A sand mandala can take several days or even weeks of work and is swept away in the end all the same.
Borobudur is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

teile.einleitung: Mary was the mother of Jesus. She is especially honoured in Christianity, and in Islam too she has a place of honour under the name Maryam.
wichtigste: Mary lived about 2000 years ago in Galilee, in the area of present-day Israel.
She was engaged to Joseph and became the mother of Jesus.
The Bible tells how the angel Gabriel announced the birth of Jesus to her.
In the Catholic and Orthodox churches, Mary is especially honoured.
In the Quran she is called Maryam, and a whole sura is named after her.

abschnitte.text: According to the **Gospels**, Mary lived in **Nazareth** in Galilee. She was engaged to the carpenter **Joseph**. The angel **Gabriel** appeared to her and announced that she would be the mother of the Son of God. This event is called the **Annunciation**. According to tradition, Jesus was born in Bethlehem. The Bible also tells that Mary was present at the cross when Jesus died.

In the **Catholic** and **Orthodox** churches, Mary is especially honoured as the “Mother of God”. Many people pray the **Hail Mary**, a prayer that begins with the angel’s greeting. There are many feasts of Mary, for example the **Assumption of Mary** on 15 August. The Reformed churches respect Mary as a role model of faith, but do not venerate her in this way.

In the **Quran** too, Mary is greatly honoured. There she is called **Maryam**. A whole sura, that is, a chapter of the Quran, bears her name. She is the only woman mentioned by name in the Quran. For Muslims, Jesus, called Isa in Arabic, is an important prophet, but not the Son of God.

In Switzerland there are many churches and chapels dedicated to Mary. A well-known place of pilgrimage is **Einsiedeln** Abbey in the canton of Schwyz, with the **Black Madonna**. Many people make a pilgrimage there every year. The first name Maria and forms of it such as Marie or Mia are also very common.

gewusst: Mary is the only woman mentioned by her name in the Quran.
The Black Madonna of Einsiedeln is a wooden figure that turned dark over a long time from candle smoke.

teile.einleitung: The Abbey Library of St Gallen is one of the oldest and most famous libraries in the world. It is part of the old monastery in St Gallen. Its magnificent Baroque hall and its ancient manuscripts attract visitors from all over the world.
wichtigste: The Abbey Library belongs to the former monastery of St Gallen.
It is one of the oldest libraries in the world.
The oldest books are over 1,000 years old and written by hand on parchment.
The great hall is decorated in the Baroque style.
Visitors wear felt slippers to protect the old wooden floor.
Since 1983 the abbey precinct has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

abschnitte.text: In the 7th century the monk **Gallus** lived as a hermit by the river Steinach. In the 8th century Otmar founded a **monastery** at this place. Over the centuries the monks collected and wrote many books. From this arose the **Abbey Library**. It is one of the oldest libraries in the world that still stands on the same spot. The city of St Gallen is named after Gallus.

The oldest books in the library are over **1,000 years** old. At that time there was no printing yet. Monks wrote every book **by hand**, letter by letter. They wrote on **parchment**, which is made from animal skin and lasts a very long time. Many pages are decorated with colourful pictures and gold paint. The library owns over 2,000 such manuscripts.

The great hall was built in the 18th century in the **Baroque** style. It has a lot of carved wood, gold and painted ceilings. Above the door is a Greek saying, often translated as **pharmacy of the soul**. What is meant is that books do the soul good as medicine does the body. Because the wooden floor is very old and valuable, all visitors pull **felt slippers** over their shoes.

In the Abbey Library lies an **Egyptian mummy**. It is the mummy of a woman named **Shepenese**. She lived over 2,500 years ago in Egypt. In the 19th century she came to St Gallen. For many children she is the most exciting part of the visit.

Since **1983** the **abbey precinct** with church and library has been a **UNESCO World Heritage Site**. In this way it is protected as especially valuable for the whole of humankind. The collection also includes the famous **Plan of St Gallen**. It shows an ideal plan for a monastery and dates from the 9th century.

gewusst: The Plan of St Gallen from the 9th century is regarded as the oldest surviving building plan of the Middle Ages.
In a library full of books lies a real Egyptian mummy.

teile.einleitung: You can often recognise Buddhist monks by their robes. Depending on the country, they are orange, dark red or black. The robe shows that a monk lives simply and gives up possessions.
wichtigste: In Thailand, Sri Lanka and Myanmar many monks wear orange or saffron-yellow robes.
Tibetan monks mostly wear dark red robes.
Zen monks in Japan often wear black robes.
A monk’s robe in Thailand usually consists of three cloths.
In the past the robes were sewn from scraps of cloth.
Buddhist monks shave their heads.
A young monk who is still learning is called a novice.

abschnitte.text: The colour of the robe is not the same everywhere. In **Thailand**, **Sri Lanka** and **Myanmar** you see many monks in **orange** or saffron-yellow cloths. In **Tibet** the monks mostly wear **dark red** robes, often together with yellow cloths. Among the **Zen monks** in Japan the robes are often **black**. So the colour depends on the country and the tradition.

A monk in Thailand usually has **three parts**: an inner robe, an outer robe and a cloak. The cloths are not put on like a shirt, but **wrapped** around the body. In the past monks sewed their robes from old **scraps of cloth**. They were meant to live simply and own nothing expensive. To this day the pattern of many robes recalls pieces sewn together.

Buddhist monks **shave their heads**. This shows that appearance is not important to them. They own only a few things. In Thailand they go through the streets early in the morning with an **alms bowl**. People give them food. For the faithful this is a good deed, and the monks do not have to do their own shopping.

A young monk who is still learning is called a **novice**. In Thailand and Myanmar many boys become novices for a few weeks or months. In the monastery they learn the teaching of Buddha, pray and meditate. Afterwards many return to their usual life. Novices too wear a simple robe and have a shaved head.

gewusst: There are Buddhist monasteries in Switzerland too, for example a Thai monastery in Gretzenbach in the canton of Solothurn.
In the past the colour of the robes often came from plant dyes such as saffron or tree bark.

teile.einleitung: Many religions and cultures celebrate festivals of lights, especially in winter. When the days are short and dark, candles and lamps bring light and hope. Whether Hanukkah, Advent, Diwali or the Lucia festival: light stands for what is good.
wichtigste: In winter the days are short and dark, which is why festivals of lights are celebrated.
Jews celebrate Hanukkah, Christians Advent.
Diwali is the great festival of lights of the Hindus.
At Diwali small oil lamps are set out.
An Advent wreath usually has four candles.
In Sweden the Lucia festival is celebrated on 13 December.

abschnitte.text: In **winter** it gets dark early, and the nights are long. For a very long time people have lit fires, candles and lamps then. The light brings **warmth** and **hope** into the dark season. That is why many religions celebrate **festivals of lights** in winter. What they all have in common is that light is a sign of the good, which is stronger than the darkness.

The Jewish festival of lights **Hanukkah** lasts eight days. It recalls an **oil miracle** in the Temple in Jerusalem: according to tradition, the oil that should have lasted for one day lasted much longer. Each evening one more candle is lit. There is a special candelabrum for this, the **hanukkiah**. Children play with a spinning top and eat foods fried in oil.

In **Advent** Christians prepare for **Christmas**, the festival of the birth of **Jesus**. An **Advent wreath** usually has **four candles**, one for each Sunday of Advent. Every Sunday one more candle is lit. At Christmas many lights shine on the tree. They recall that for Christians Jesus is the light of the world.

**Diwali** is the great festival of lights of the **Hindus**. It is celebrated in autumn, usually in October or November. People set out many small clay **oil lamps** in and in front of their houses. They stand for the victory of light over darkness. People decorate their houses, wear new clothes and eat sweets.

In **Sweden** the **Lucia festival** is celebrated on **13 December**. A girl in a white dress wears a wreath of candles on her head. The festival recalls **Saint Lucia**. In Switzerland, children walk through the streets in November in the **Räbeliechtli procession** with hollowed-out, lit turnips and sing as they go.

gewusst: The name Lucia comes from the Latin word “lux”, which means light.
The candelabrum for Hanukkah has nine arms: eight for the days of the festival and one for the candle with which the others are lit.

teile.einleitung: The Pali Canon is the oldest completely preserved collection of Buddhist writings. It is written in the Pali language and is the sacred scripture of Theravada Buddhism.
wichtigste: The Pali Canon is also called the Tipitaka, which means “Three Baskets”.
The Vinaya Pitaka contains the rules of the order for monks and nuns.
The Sutta Pitaka contains Buddha’s discourses, including the Dhammapada.
The Abhidhamma Pitaka analyses the teaching systematically.
In the 1st century BC the canon was first written down in Sri Lanka.
Pali is one of the Middle Indo-Aryan languages.

abschnitte.text: The Pali Canon is divided into three collections. They are called **baskets**, in Pali **pitaka**. This is where the name **Tipitaka** comes from, in Sanskrit **Tripitaka**. Each basket contains a different kind of text. Together they form a very large collection.

The **Vinaya Pitaka** collects the rules for the life of monks and nuns and tells how these rules came about. The **Sutta Pitaka** contains the discourses of Buddha. It includes the well-known collection of verses, the **Dhammapada**, in the “Minor Collection”. The **Abhidhamma Pitaka** arranges the teaching in lists and examines the human mind. It is regarded as the youngest basket.

According to tradition, after Buddha’s death his disciples met at the **first council** in Rajagaha. There **Ananda**, Buddha’s companion of many years, recited the discourses. **Upali** recited the rules of the order. For a long time the texts were passed on only by word of mouth, and monks learned them by heart.

In the **1st century BC**, according to the chronicles of Sri Lanka, monks wrote down the canon for the first time. This happened in the monastery of **Aluvihara**, on **palm leaves**. The language **Pali** is a Middle Indo-Aryan language, related to the Prakrit languages. Today it is used mainly as a sacred language.

**Theravada**, which is widespread in Sri Lanka, Thailand, Myanmar, Laos and Cambodia, is based on the Pali Canon. Other branches of Buddhism use mainly Chinese and Tibetan collections of writings. Monks still recite texts from the Pali Canon in their prayers today.

gewusst: In Mandalay in Myanmar, the whole Pali Canon was carved into more than 700 marble slabs in the 19th century.
A “sutta” is a discourse, and the word corresponds to the Sanskrit word “sutra”.

teile.einleitung: The new year does not begin on 1 January everywhere. Different religions and cultures have their own calendars and their own New Year festivals. Some celebrate in autumn, others in spring.
wichtigste: The Jewish New Year is called Rosh Hashanah and falls in autumn.
On Rosh Hashanah people eat apple with honey and blow the shofar.
The Islamic calendar follows the moon and begins with Muhammad’s emigration in 622.
The Christian church year begins with the first Sunday of Advent.
Nowruz is celebrated around 21 March at the start of spring.
In Thailand people splash each other with water at Songkran in April.
New Year’s Eve is called Silvester in German, after Pope Sylvester I.

abschnitte.text: The Jewish New Year is called **Rosh Hashanah**, which means “head of the year”. It is celebrated in **autumn**, in September or early October. People dip **pieces of apple in honey** and wish each other a sweet new year. In the synagogue the **shofar**, a ram’s horn, is blown. Its loud note is meant to wake people up and make them think.

The **Islamic calendar** follows the **moon**. A lunar year is about 11 days shorter than a solar year. That is why the Islamic New Year falls about 11 days earlier every year. The calendar begins with the **Hijra**: in the year 622 the Prophet **Muhammad** emigrated with his followers **from Mecca to Medina**.

abschnitte.titel: Church year and New Year’s Eve
abschnitte.text: The Christian **church year** does not begin on 1 January, but with the **first Sunday of Advent**, four Sundays before Christmas. The civil year ends on 31 December, **Silvester** in German. The name comes from **Pope Sylvester I**, who died on 31 December 335. In Switzerland there are special customs at the turn of the year, for example **Silvesterklausen** in Appenzell Ausserrhoden.

**Nowruz** means “new day”. It is celebrated around **21 March**, when spring begins. Nowruz is especially important in **Iran**, but also in Afghanistan, among the Kurds and in Central Asia. In **Thailand** the New Year is called **Songkran** and falls in **April**. People cheerfully splash each other with water. Water stands for cleansing and good luck.

The **Chinese New Year** also follows a lunar calendar. It always falls on a day between 21 January and 20 February. Each year belongs to one of twelve **zodiac animals**, for example the dragon or the rabbit. People celebrate with family, fireworks and lucky red colours. It is the most important family festival in China.

gewusst: Nowruz has been on UNESCO’s list of intangible cultural heritage since 2009.
In Appenzell Ausserrhoden, New Year’s Eve is celebrated twice: on 31 December and, by the old calendar, on 13 January.

teile.einleitung: Orthodox Judaism is the branch of Judaism that holds especially strictly to the traditional commandments. Its followers live their everyday lives by Jewish religious law, the **Halakha**.
wichtigste: For Orthodox Jews, God gave the Torah to Moses on Mount Sinai.
The commandments of the Torah therefore apply to them unchanged.
On the Sabbath, Orthodox Jews do not drive and do not use electrical devices.
In Orthodox synagogues men and women sit separately.
Very strictly observant ultra-Orthodox Jews are called Haredim in Hebrew.
Orthodox Jews eat only food that is kosher according to the dietary laws.

abschnitte.text: At the centre is the **Torah**, the five books of Moses. For Orthodox Judaism, God gave it to Moses on Mount **Sinai**. This also includes the oral tradition, which was later written down in the **Talmud**. Because the commandments come from God, people may not simply change them. But rabbis interpret them for new questions, for example about modern technology.

The **Sabbath** begins on Friday evening and ends on Saturday evening. On this day of rest, many kinds of work are forbidden by religious law, including making a fire. That is why Orthodox Jews do not drive a car or switch on a light. Many walk to the synagogue. The day belongs to prayer, family and shared meals.

In Orthodox synagogues men and women sit in separate areas. There is often a **women’s gallery** or a partition called a **mechitza**. The service is held mainly in Hebrew. During prayer men wear a head covering, the **kippah**, and often a prayer shawl.

Orthodox Judaism is not uniform. The **Haredim**, which means “those who fear God”, live very strictly and often wear dark clothes. **Modern Orthodoxy** combines the commandments with a life in the middle of today’s society, with work and study. In Switzerland too, for example in Zurich and Basel, there are Orthodox communities.

The dietary laws are called **kashrut**. Permitted food is called **kosher**. Pork, for example, is forbidden. Meat and milk are not eaten together, and in Orthodox kitchens they are often even prepared with separate dishes.

gewusst: In some residential districts, Orthodox communities stretch a wire, the eruv. Within it, things may be carried on the Sabbath.
There are special Sabbath lifts that stop by themselves at every floor, so that nobody has to press a button.

teile.einleitung: The Easter fire is part of the Easter Vigil service in many Catholic churches. It is lit in front of the church and stands for Jesus Christ, who, according to Christian belief, rose from the dead.
wichtigste: The Easter fire burns on the night of Easter Vigil in front of many Catholic churches.
The priest blesses the fire.
The large Easter candle is lit from the Easter fire.
The light is then carried into the dark church.
The fire stands for the light that overcomes the darkness.

abschnitte.text: The **Easter Vigil** is the night before Easter Sunday. The service begins in the dark in front of the church. There the **Easter fire** burns, which the priest blesses. For Christians the fire shows that Jesus has defeated death, just as light drives away the night.

The large **Easter candle** is lit from the Easter fire. It bears a cross, the year and the Greek letters **alpha and omega**, the first and the last letter. The priest carries the candle into the dark church. People light their small candles from it, until the whole church is bright.

Outside the church too there are fires at Easter. In some areas, for example in northern Germany, large heaps of wood are lit, and many people gather around them. In many Catholic parishes in Switzerland, the fire in front of the church is a fixed part of the Easter Vigil.

gewusst: The Easter candle then burns all year at baptisms and at funeral services in the church.

teile.einleitung: Religions have signs by which they can be recognised. You see such symbols on churches, synagogues, mosques or temples, but also on jewellery and flags. Many have a long history.
wichtigste: The most important symbol of Christians is the **cross**.
The **Star of David** with six points is a sign of Judaism.
The **menorah** is a candelabrum with seven arms.
The **crescent** is a well-known sign of Islam.
The **wheel of the teaching** with eight spokes stands for Buddhism.
The first Christians recognised each other by the sign of the fish.

abschnitte.text: The **cross** recalls that Jesus died on the cross. For Christians it is also a sign of hope. The first Christians used the **fish** as a secret sign of recognition. The Greek word for fish is “Ichthys”, and its letters are the beginnings of the words “Jesus Christ, God’s Son, Saviour”. The **dove** stands for the Holy Spirit and is today a sign of peace all over the world.

The **Star of David** is named after King David. It consists of two triangles lying on top of each other and has six points. You can also see it on the flag of Israel. Older still is the **menorah**, a candelabrum with seven arms that once stood in the Temple in Jerusalem.

The **crescent**, often with a star, has become a well-known sign of Islam. You see it on many minarets. The Red Cross movement was founded by the Genevan **Henri Dunant**. In many Muslim countries it is called the **Red Crescent** and uses this sign instead of the cross.

Buddhism has the **wheel of the teaching** as its sign. It recalls the teaching of the Buddha, and its eight spokes stand for the **Noble Eightfold Path**. In Hinduism the sacred syllable **Om** is an important sign. The Sikhs have the Khanda, a sign with a double-edged sword in the middle.

gewusst: The Red Cross emblem came from the Swiss flag with its colours reversed, as an honour to Switzerland.
The menorah is shown on the coat of arms of the State of Israel.

teile.einleitung: Einsiedeln Abbey in the canton of Schwyz is one of the best-known monasteries in Switzerland. Benedictine monks live here, and many pilgrims come every year. Einsiedeln is the largest place of pilgrimage in Switzerland.
wichtigste: Einsiedeln lies in the canton of Schwyz.
The place is named after the hermit Meinrad, who lived here in the forest.
Two ravens can be seen in the coat of arms of the abbey and the village.
The abbey is led by an abbot, whom the monks elect.
Einsiedeln is the largest place of pilgrimage in Switzerland.
The abbey has a very old stud farm for horses.
A well-known pastry is the Einsiedeln ram.

abschnitte.text: More than 1,100 years ago the monk **Meinrad** withdrew into the dark forest. He lived there alone and prayed. A person who lives alone like this is called a **hermit**, in German “Einsiedler”. That is why the place later received the name **Einsiedeln**. Meinrad is revered today as a saint.

A legend tells that two **ravens** lived with Meinrad. After his death they are said to have pursued the culprits until they were caught. That is why the **coats of arms** of the abbey and the village show two ravens. You can still see them in many places in Einsiedeln.

In the 10th century a **Benedictine abbey** arose at Meinrad’s place. It is led by an **abbot**, whom the monks elect themselves. The large **abbey church** was built in the 18th century in the **Baroque** style and is splendidly decorated inside. In the Chapel of Grace stands the famous **Black Madonna**, a figure of Mary with a dark face.

abschnitte.titel: Pilgrims from all over the world
abschnitte.text: Einsiedeln is the largest **place of pilgrimage** in Switzerland. Every year very many **pilgrims** come to pray in the church. The place also lies on the **Way of St James**, which leads as far as Spain. Many pilgrims take home a **ram** as a souvenir, a gingerbread pastry in the shape of a ram.

For many hundreds of years the monks have bred **horses**. The stud farm is regarded as the oldest still existing stud farm in Europe. The abbey also has a **monastery school**, that is, a secondary school, and a large library. The monks work, pray and study according to the rule of Saint Benedict.

gewusst: The horses from Einsiedeln are also called “Cavalli della Madonna”, horses of the Mother of God.
Fahr Abbey on the Limmat also belongs to Einsiedeln Abbey.

teile.einleitung: Orphism was a religious movement in ancient Greece. It is named after the mythical singer Orpheus. The Orphics believed in an immortal soul that wanders through many lives.
wichtigste: Orphism is named after the singer Orpheus.
The sacred writings of the Orphics were attributed to him.
The formula “soma sema” means: the body is a tomb of the soul.
The Orphics believed in a cycle of rebirths.
Many gave up eating meat.
Gold leaves from graves give the dead advice for the underworld.
The Derveni Papyrus is regarded as the oldest surviving book in Europe.

abschnitte.text: In Greek legend **Orpheus** was a **singer** with a divine gift. With his music he is said to have moved even animals, trees and stones. He went down into the **underworld** to bring back his dead wife Eurydice. The **Orphics** saw him as their teacher. They attributed their sacred poems and writings to him.

The Orphics believed that the **soul is immortal**. According to their teaching, it wanders through several bodies. This is called a **cycle of rebirths**. The formula **“soma sema”** is well known: the body is a tomb of the soul. The philosopher **Plato** takes up this play on words in the dialogue “Cratylus”. Through a pure life the soul could free itself from the cycle.

The **Orphic life** involved fixed rules. Because the soul could also live in animals, many Orphics gave up **meat**. They therefore also avoided bloody **sacrifices**, which were otherwise usual in Greece. In this way they wanted to stay pure. Similar ideas are found among the followers of Pythagoras.

An important Orphic myth tells of the **child Dionysus**. The **Titans**, an old race of gods, killed him. **Zeus** punished them and burned them with his **lightning bolt**. According to the myth, humans arose from their **ashes**. That is why a human being carries both a Titanic and a divine inheritance. The divine part is the soul, which is to be set free.

In graves, thin, inscribed **gold leaves** were found. They give the dead advice for the underworld. They warn against the **spring of forgetfulness**. The dead person should instead drink from the spring of **Mnemosyne**, the goddess of memory. In 1962 the **Derveni Papyrus** was found in a grave near **Thessaloniki**. It contains a commentary on an Orphic poem about the origin of the gods and is regarded as the **oldest surviving book in Europe**.

gewusst: The Derveni Papyrus survived only because it was partly charred on a funeral pyre.
The myth of Orpheus inspired many operas, including one of the very first operas, “L’Orfeo” by Claudio Monteverdi.

teile.einleitung: In the belief of the Andean peoples of South America, Pachamama is Mother Earth. She gives good harvests and is still revered today by many people in Peru, Bolivia, Ecuador and other countries.
wichtigste: Pachamama means Mother Earth.
The Quechua word “pacha” means world, earth and time all at once, and “mama” means mother.
August is regarded as the month of Pachamama.
Offerings are placed in a hole in the ground to “feed” the earth.
The maize drink chicha is a popular offering.
In 2008 Ecuador wrote the rights of nature into its constitution, and in 2010 Bolivia passed a law on the rights of Mother Earth.

abschnitte.text: For the **Quechua** and **Aymara** peoples the earth is alive. Pachamama gives people food, water and fertility for the fields. That is why one should thank her and not exploit her. The Aymara live mainly around **Lake Titicaca** in Bolivia and Peru.

Families dig a hole in the ground and fill it with food, drink and **coca leaves**. In this way, according to belief, the earth is “fed”. Before drinking, many people pour a few drops of **chicha** on the ground. Chicha is a drink made from maize. In this way Mother Earth gets the first sip.

In the Andes, **August** is the month of Pachamama. Then, according to belief, the earth is hungry and waits for gifts before sowing. During this time many communities hold special rituals. People often combine these old customs with Christian belief.

Alongside Pachamama, people revere the **Apus**. These are the spirits of the mountains, which according to belief live in the high peaks. They protect the people, animals and fields in their surroundings. Gifts are brought to them too.

The ideas around Pachamama have even shaped laws. In 2008 **Ecuador** became the first country to write the rights of nature into its constitution, and there it also calls her Pacha Mama. In 2010 **Bolivia** passed a law on the rights of Mother Earth. It describes the earth as a living system with rights of its own.

gewusst: Under the constitution of Ecuador, the rights of nature can be enforced in court.
The word “pacha” means space and time at once, that is, the whole world.

teile.einleitung: Mana is a word from languages of the Pacific islands. In the anthropology of religion it means an impersonal supernatural force that can work in people, things or places.
wichtigste: Mana comes from languages of Melanesia and Polynesia in the Pacific.
It means an impersonal, supernatural power.
The missionary Robert Henry Codrington made the term known in Europe in 1891.
Robert Ranulph Marett developed from it the theory of pre-animism.
Marcel Mauss and Henri Hubert saw in mana a key to magic.

abschnitte.text: On many islands in the Pacific, people believed in a special force called **mana**. It makes a person successful and powerful. A chief, a warrior or a special object can have a lot of mana. Mana is **impersonal**: it is not a god and not a spirit, but a kind of effective power.

The English missionary **Robert Henry Codrington** described mana in 1891 in his book “The Melanesians”. After that, scholars took over the term. They also used it for similar ideas in other cultures. In this way mana became a technical word of the **anthropology of religion**, the science of the religions of different peoples.

The scholar **Edward Tylor** thought that religion begins with belief in souls, **animism**. **Robert Ranulph Marett** disagreed: before that, he said, there had been a feeling for an impersonal power such as mana. This earlier stage he called **pre-animism**. The French scholars **Marcel Mauss** and **Henri Hubert** interpreted mana around 1903 as an idea that makes magical action seem effective. Today many researchers view such stage models critically.

gewusst: In many computer games the magic power of a character is called “mana”. The word originally comes from the Pacific.
The anthropologist Claude Lévi-Strauss called mana an “empty signifier”, that is, a word that can take on almost any meaning.

teile.einleitung: In the fasting month of Ramadan, devout Muslims eat and drink nothing during the day. That is why the meal before sunrise is especially important. It is called Sahur.
wichtigste: **Sahur** is the meal before dawn in Ramadan.
After it you eat and drink nothing more until sunset.
In the evening the fast is broken with the **iftar**.
**Ramadan** is the ninth month of the Islamic calendar.
Children, the sick and travellers do not have to fast.

abschnitte.text: **Ramadan** is the ninth month of the Islamic calendar. Fasting in this month is one of the five pillars of Islam, its most important duties. From dawn until sunset, believers eat and drink nothing. Because the Islamic calendar follows the moon, Ramadan moves through the seasons. Children, the sick, the elderly and travellers are excused from fasting.

For **Sahur**, many families get up in the middle of the night or very early in the morning. The meal must be finished before dawn, when the first prayer of the day begins. People eat food that keeps them full for a long time and drink plenty of water. In some countries, drummers used to go through the streets, and in places still do, to wake people for Sahur.

At sunset the fast is broken with the **iftar**. Often people first eat a date and drink water. A larger meal follows, frequently with family, friends and neighbours. In Switzerland too, mosques and associations sometimes invite people to a shared iftar during Ramadan, including people of other religions.

gewusst: In Switzerland a day of fasting lasts much longer in summer than in winter, because the sun is in the sky for longer.

teile.einleitung: In ancient Egypt, Maat is both a goddess and an important idea. She stands for truth, justice and the right order of the world. Maat also played a large part in the judgement of the dead.
wichtigste: Maat stands for truth, justice and world order.
The goddess Maat wears an ostrich feather on her head.
At the judgement of the dead, the heart is weighed against the feather of Maat.
The composite creature Ammit devours the heart of a guilty dead person.
The opposite of Maat is called Isfet.
The pharaoh had to bring Maat about on earth.

abschnitte.text: **Maat** means the right **order** of the world, of society and of action. This includes **truth** and **justice**. The goddess Maat embodies this principle. She was regarded as the daughter of the sun god **Re**, who set up the world order at the creation. It was even said that Re lives on Maat.

The mark of the goddess is an **ostrich feather** on her head. The feather also serves as the **hieroglyph**, that is, the written sign, for her name. In pictures Maat is often seen as a seated woman with this feather. Sometimes she also has wings on her arms.

According to Egyptian belief, every dead person had to face a **judgement of the dead**. In it his **heart** was weighed on a scale against the **feather of Maat**. The heart was regarded as the seat of the **conscience**. If it was no heavier than the feather, the dead person was allowed to enter the **afterlife**. Otherwise **Ammit** devoured it, a composite creature of crocodile, lion and hippopotamus, and the dead person was destroyed for ever.

In the **Book of the Dead** there are spells for the way into the afterlife. In **Spell 125** the dead person declares before **42 judges of the dead** that he has not committed certain wrongs. He says, for example, that he has not stolen and not lied. This declaration is called the **negative confession**. In this way the dead person showed that he had lived according to Maat.

The opposite of Maat is called **Isfet**. It stands for **chaos**, injustice, lies and violence. The task of the **pharaoh** was to bring Maat about on earth and to drive out Isfet. The king was regarded as the guarantor of the world order. In rituals he presented the gods with a small **figure of Maat** as an offering.

gewusst: Many pictures of the judgement of the dead survive on papyrus scrolls that were laid in the grave with the dead.
The name Maat is found in royal names too: the female pharaoh Hatshepsut had the throne name Maatkare.

teile.einleitung: The Kumbh Mela is a great Hindu pilgrimage festival in India. Millions of people bathe in holy rivers during it. It is regarded as the largest religious gathering in the world.
wichtigste: At the Kumbh Mela pilgrims bathe in holy rivers to cleanse themselves of sins.
The festival takes place in turn in Prayagraj, Haridwar, Ujjain and Nashik.
“Kumbh” means pitcher.
